text:
We have never stayed in accommodation that was this dirty. The location itself is beautiful, and thankfully, the air conditioning worked.

Only Mimi speaks English; unfortunately, no one else does. Whenever we wanted to order something, we had to use hand gestures and try to explain what we wanted. The food is not recommended either, so we ended up walking to a resort further down the beach to eat.

There were insects everywhere in our room, including biting ants, mosquitoes, and spiders. The bathroom had clumps of hair left behind by previous guests, and judging by the overall condition of the room, it was clear that it had not been properly cleaned.

The water smelled strongly of sewage, which was extremely unpleasant.

The beach loungers are made of bare wood with no cushions, making them very uncomfortable to lie on.

Overall, this place is far too expensive for what you get. The property is in serious need of renovation and, in our opinion, should either be properly renovated or closed until it meets basic standards.

We also did not feel particularly welcomed by the staff. Most of the time, the staff were either sleeping in the hammocks or sitting on their phones. If you decide to stay here, be prepared for very limited English communication and a lack of service.

The location is beautiful, and the air conditioning worked, but unfortunately, those are the only positives we can mention. For the price, we expected much more.

textTranslated:
Mixed feelings about our visit to the Perhentian Islands. The nature is overwhelmingly beautiful. The resort is beautifully situated in Turtle Bay. The basic amenities are all present at the resort.

However, the quality of the resort is mediocre. The bungalows are somewhat outdated, and we had cockroaches visiting us several evenings. We stayed for 5 nights; the toilet and shower were not cleaned a single time (although the bungalow was swept daily, beds were made, and fresh towels and toilet paper were replenished). The staff were only moderately helpful with questions, and the restaurant was of reasonable quality.

Animals belong in a jungle, and it is nice that lizards, monkeys, geckos, and squirrels roam around with them. We enjoyed that.

Incidentally, you can simply pay with your credit card (at almost all restaurants on the island). Boat service to the other beaches or Kecil is quick and easy (pay in cash for this). Tip: if you want to drink wine, bring it with you from the mainland.

text: I want to be fair. Perhaps this would have been a wonderful experience for a young family, if they are OK with very “rustic” accommodations. We are not that young family. We paid $800 ringgit per night for what we believed would be at least an adequate resort (in Kuala Lumpur, that same $800 would have more than paid for a suite in a 5-star hotel). Our expectations were not super high, since we understood that we were paying for an experience on a private island. Just clean and comfortable. Unfortunately, we got neither. Our room, #208 had a broken front door that only opened 1/3 of the way, scraping across the floor and then stopping. There were deep gouges and white paint all over the floor, which let us know this issue is ongoing. At first glance, the room looked clean (and bedding was fresh), but on further inspection we could see that only surface cleaning has ever been done. The doors were filthy, mold stains on walls, absolute filth in the pipes and shower drain and air conditioning filters. Dirty, streaked mirrors. Also, the king size bed was hard as a rock - extremely uncomfortable with a poor quality mattress. We paid an extra $100 ringgit for an “extra bed” which was just a cot - a plastic mattress. Food at PIR is bad and obscenely expensive. Piles of trash behind convenience stores and coffee shops. And overall, a deeply unpleasant sewage smell in our room and permeating the island. The good: beach is absolutely lovely. Water is crystal clear, sand is white. No trash on the beach (they hide trash behind businesses, but it’s obvious as it stinks and attracts rodents). It was a wonderful experience to swim with colorful tropical fish. That was the one and only thing I appreciated about this overpriced and horrifically maintained island.

text:
Je suis très très très mitigée sur cet hôtel.

La plage est terriblement belle et l’hôtel terriblement vétuste. Je suis passée de l’ébahissement au dégoût tout au long de mon séjour.

La première certitude c’est qu’en séjournant là, il faut être très très à l’aise avec la faune: jeckos, lézards, fourmis, sauterelles, écureuils qui ressemblent à des rats, varans et même des varans malais. Dans la chambre, il y a tout de même une mise en garde contre toute cette faune et également contre des serpents. Sincèrement, nous n’en avons pas vu. Mais toutes ces bêtes sont omniprésentes. Donc j’ai passé un séjour en état d’alerte maximum 🤣

Ensuite, la chambre est crade au possible, elle sent les égouts et le linge de lit et de bain est… piteux. Troué, taché, jaune… j’ai mis des photos mais l’insalubrité générale de l’hôtel est indescriptible. Les transats à la plage sont des planches en bois sans matelas et il n’y a pas de parasols. Si vous vous mettez sous les palmiers, prenez garde aux écureuils qui en ont terrifié certains.
Pour finir, le petit déjeuner est très sommaire, le café indéfinissable: noir pétrole mais absolument aucun goût de café. Le resto du soir était sincèrement correct. Il n’y a rien à faire le soir, prévoyez un IPad et une connexion 4/5G qui fonctionne très bien. Il n’y a pas de wifi.

Quant à la plage… waouh! La plus belle de Perhentian. On a nagé quotidiennement avec des raies, des tortues, des bébés requins etc

Il y a plein de gens qui viennent à la journée (c’est le défilé des bateaux par contre) et je me demande si ce n’est pas ce qu’il faut faire en réalité. Bref.

Aussi je ne déconseillerais pas d’y aller vu la magie de la plage mais d’y aller en connaissance de cause et en payant le bon prix car moi, j’ai payé sur Agoda/Booking plus de 300€ la nuit et à ce prix là, c’est sincèrement du vol manifeste.
textTranslated:
I have very, very mixed feelings about this hotel.

The beach is stunningly beautiful, but the hotel is terribly run-down. I went from being amazed to disgusted throughout my stay.

The first thing to know is that if you stay there, you have to be very, very comfortable with the wildlife: jeckos, lizards, ants, grasshoppers, squirrels that look like rats, monitor lizards, and even Malayan water lizards. In the room, there's a warning about all this wildlife and also about snakes. Honestly, we didn't see any. But all these creatures are everywhere. So I spent my stay on high alert 🤣

Then, the room is filthy, it smells like sewage, and the bed linens and towels are... pathetic. Torn, stained, yellowed… I've included photos, but the overall unsanitary condition of the hotel is indescribable. The beach chairs are wooden planks without mattresses, and there are no parasols. If you sit under the palm trees, beware of the squirrels; some people have been terrified.

Finally, breakfast is very basic, and the coffee is indescribable: black as petrol, with absolutely no coffee flavor. The dinner restaurant was honestly decent. There's nothing to do in the evenings, so bring an iPad and a 4G/5G connection, which works very well. There's no Wi-Fi.

As for the beach… wow! The most beautiful on Perhentian. We swam daily with rays, turtles, baby sharks, etc.

Lots of people come for the day (it's a constant parade of boats, though), and I wonder if that's not what you should really be doing. Anyway.

So, I wouldn't advise against going, given the magic of the beach, but go with full awareness and pay the right price because I paid over €300 a night on Agoda/Booking, and at that price, it's frankly highway robbery.

text: Abbiamo passato in questo resort 5 giorni e 4 notti. Per iniziare devo dire che abbiamo sognato le isole perenthian per mesi, e devo dire che non deludono le aspettative, sono un paradiso incontaminata! Siamo però partiti un pò scoraggiati dalle recensioni delle varie strutture e dopo un annetto di ricerca conveniamo nel prenotare al PIR camera beach front. Capitolo posizione: sicuramente la spiaggia piu bella di tutte e due le isole, la spiaggia si trova a Besar(isola grande), posizione eccellente, turtle point a 50 m dalla riva. Tutti i giorni abbiamo fatto il bagno in mezzo a pesci di ogni specie,  razze e tanti squaletti pinna nera che venivano regolarmente a trovarci, sensazione meravigliosa! Capitolo camera: la camera beach front è sicuramente la migliore del resort,  abbiamo scelto il pacchetto colazione inclusa, la camera è in legno, sicuramente no  di lusso ma direi che le assegnerei 3 stelle. Comunque dispone di questa balconata fronte mare, ogni mattina ci siamo svegliati con il rumore del mare praticamente a 30 secondi di distanza da noi. Camera in sostanza pulita, ovviamente bisogna tenere presente che si è su un isola abbastanza selvaggia  in malesia. Capitolo servizi; i ragazzi che lavorano al PIR sono tutti gentilissimi e cordiali, sicuramente metterei piu lettini sulla spiaggia e magari una tipologia piu comoda, ma che te ne fai dei lettini quando hai quella sabbia paradisiaca? Capitolo cibo: la colazione del PIR era abbastanza fornita con una buona scelta internazionale e soprattutto asiatica. Conclusioni: la nostra esperienza estate piu che positiva! Ovviamente bisogna tenere conto che si è su un isola selvaggia, con un mare da sogno che sicuramente non ha niente da invidiare a posti come le Maldive. Inutile cercare una servizio 5 stelle, qui si viene per distaccarsi dal mondo! Lo consiglio vivamente a chi vuole immergersi in questo paradiso.
textTranslated: We spent 5 days and 4 nights at this resort. To begin with, I must say that we had been dreaming of the Perhentian Islands for months, and I must say that they did not disappoint—they are an unspoiled paradise! However, we were a little discouraged by the reviews of the various properties, and after a year of research, we decided to book a beachfront room at the PIR. About the location: it is definitely the most beautiful beach on both islands. The beach is located on Besar (the large island), in an excellent location, with a turtle point 50 meters from the shore. Every day, we swam among fish of every species, rays, and many blacktip reef sharks that regularly came to visit us—a wonderful feeling! About the room: the beachfront room is definitely the best in the resort. We chose the breakfast-inclusive package. The room is wooden, certainly not luxurious, but I would say I'd give it 3 stars. However, it has this sea-facing balcony; every morning, we woke up to the sound of the sea practically 30 seconds away. The room was basically clean, but you have to keep in mind that you're on a fairly untamed island in Malaysia. As for the services, the staff at PIR are all incredibly kind and friendly. I'd definitely add more loungers on the beach, perhaps a more comfortable one, but what do you need loungers for when you have that heavenly sand? As for the food, the breakfast at PIR was quite extensive, with a good selection of international and especially Asian dishes. Conclusion: Our summer experience was beyond positive! Of course, you have to keep in mind that you're on a wild island, with a dreamy sea that certainly rivals places like the Maldives. There's no point in looking for 5-star service; you come here to disconnect from the world! I highly recommend it to anyone who wants to immerse themselves in this paradise.

text:
Incredible potential - very disappointing execution. If I start with the positives, the resort is situated on an incredible beach, crystal clear sea with a simple water taxi system that can take you to a number of other beautiful locations around the island. The resort itself would be best described as neglected. Full of promise and really disappointing delivery as the rooms are less than clean, with very dated bathrooms and evidence of bed bugs that had once infested the room. The rooms are very close to the beach, making the views from the balcony a bit of a bonus. The facilities in the resort were pretty rubbish to be honest, a dirty unused pool, empty games room, one set of badminton rackets for the entire hotel to share, a karaoke room that you can pay extra to use, absolutely no daytime/evening entertainment and breakfast/dinner service that was quite shocking. I wouldn’t mind having limited service but the resort advertises WiFi, then informs you on arrival that it is only available in reception - a place you probably want to avoid as much as possible. One of the reasons to travel to SE Asia is for the food, then you are met with a cold, stale selection of buffet food. The BBQ buffet somehow doubles the price of the service whilst serving much of the same food but warmed on the grill before service. I think the lowlight of the resort however has to be the service from the reception team. The ladies appeared frankly irritated during any interaction and would best be described as less than welcoming. The laundry service was not running due to “bad water”, despite it being promoted on the room information - not sure if this was a short term or long term issue they were having.

I was unfortunate enough to suffer from a series of lacerations on my hand from a quite bizarre needlefish attack, this led to significant bleeding. The receptionists were completely uninterested in helping me, nor did they demonstrate any empathy as I bled out in reception. I was lucky enough that a paramedic guest was checking in at that time and assisted me. Bizarrely, the receptionists weren’t even enthusiastic about having the blood cleaned from the floor and it dried/remained there for the final day of our stay. Their service peaked when they asked us to return the spare roll of toilet paper that we had been using to help clean up some of the spilled blood - there is no telling what they would have wanted to do with it had we obliged, which we did not.

It is hard to describe why, but the resort feels overstaffed without ever having anyone available that can help you with any of your needs. I am yet to work out why staff were distributed in a way that felt as though they were able to enjoy each others company as opposed to meeting the needs of guests. One man in the only functioning coffee shop battled away as three members of staff sat in the other cafe unable to serve due to a lack of beans. The collection of slackers appeared offended when I proposed that one of them perhaps join him in his struggle or fetch some of his beans (I even offered to undertake this 5 minute walk for them) so they might be able to serve to share the burden - their response made me feel stupid for thinking out loud.

To summarise, if spending time on a beautiful beach supplemented by poorly maintained facilities, limited selection of gross food and staff that don’t care about you is not your thing, give this place a miss!

Par où commencer….

Il est situé sur la plus belles plage de l’île où l’on peut croiser requins, raies et tortues à 5 mètres du rivage. Mais je pense que la gérance se base uniquement là dessus pour faire valoir des prix aussi élevés car l’hôtel en lui-même ne les mérite vraiment pas! En résumé, je ne sais pas si je peux vous conseiller ce logement car je pense que cela est plus agréable et pourrait revenir moins cher de loger ailleurs sur l’île et de profiter de leur plage en prenant des bateaux taxis.

Where to begin…

We were given room 228, which was separate and adjoining room 227. The walls were so thin that we were delighted to hear all the joys and sorrows of the family next door… But the main problem is the maintenance of the bungalow. Between the damp patches, the smell of sewage in the bathroom, the yellowish water coming out of the tap and shower, the termite infestations, etc., you get the feeling that the managers' main goal isn't to ensure guests have a pleasant stay. Yes, the cleaning is done (quickly) every day, and the staff tries to fix the problems, but I think the priority should be a bit of a refresh. The breakfast is okay, nothing special. The resort has some nice amenities, but the real highlight is the location. It's situated on the most beautiful beach on the island, where you can see sharks, rays, and turtles just 5 meters from the shore. But I think the management is basing their prices solely on that, because the hotel itself really doesn't deserve them! In short, I don't know if I can recommend this accommodation because I think it would be more pleasant and potentially cheaper to stay elsewhere on the island and enjoy their beach by taking water taxis.

text:
La ubicación es espectacular, pero es lo único que se salva. El estado del resort y el nivel de mantenimiento son, sencillamente, inaceptables. Este es, de largo, el peor sitio donde me he alojado, y he viajado bastante.

Para empezar, la limpieza es totalmente inexistente. Durante toda la estancia (seis días) se limitaron a cambiar las toallas y a poner botellas de agua. No limpiaron la habitación ni el cuarto de baño, ni cambiaron las sábanas. Un día olvidaron reponer el papel higiénico (tuve que ir a pedirlo a recepción); otro, vaciar la papelera y un tercer día, directamente no pasaron a "limpiar" la habitación: tuvimos que reclamarlo también.

Las instalaciones están muy deterioradas. El mobiliario es viejo, desgastado y sucio, los cristales están llenos de suciedad, la ducha necesita una renovación urgente y varios elementos de la habitación no funcionan correctamente. Además, carece de lo más básico: no hay armario ni cajones donde guardar la ropa. Por otro lado, nos encontramos dos cucarachas en el cuarto de baño. Que esto ocurra en un alojamiento que cobra estos precios es sencillamente inaceptable.

Respecto a la comida del restaurante, es cara y de bajísima calidad. El desayuno, además de escaso, ofrece una variedad mínima y todos los productos están destapados, en un sitio donde moscas y mosquitos campan a sus anchas.

Es una pena que un lugar con una ubicación tan privilegiada esté tan mal gestionado. A mí no me quedó más remedio que hacer la reserva en este sitio porque, por circunstancias, miré los alojamientos tarde y solo quedaba una habitación en este. Por eso, recomiendo encarecidamente a quien tenga pensado pasar unos días en Perhentian que reserve con mucha antelación para que no le ocurra lo mismo que a nosotr@s. Sería una lástima que lo que puede ser una  experiencia inolvidable en unas playas paradisíacas se convierta en inolvidable por motivos muy distintos.
textTranslated:
The location is spectacular, but that's the only redeeming feature. The state of the resort and the level of maintenance are simply unacceptable. This is, by far, the worst place I've ever stayed, and I've traveled quite a bit.

To begin with, the cleaning is completely nonexistent. During our entire stay (six days), they only changed the towels and provided bottled water. They didn't clean the room or the bathroom, nor did they change the sheets. One day they forgot to replenish the toilet paper (I had to go to reception to ask for it); another day, they forgot to empty the trash can; and on a third day, they simply didn't come to "clean" the room: we had to complain about that too.

The facilities are very run-down. The furniture is old, worn, and dirty; the windows are covered in grime; the shower desperately needs replacing; and several things in the room don't work properly. Furthermore, it lacks the most basic amenities: there's no wardrobe or drawers to store clothes. On top of that, we found two cockroaches in the bathroom. That this happens at a hotel charging these prices is simply unacceptable.

Regarding the restaurant food, it's expensive and of extremely poor quality. The breakfast, besides being meager, offers minimal variety, and all the items are left uncovered in a place where flies and mosquitoes are rampant.

It's a shame that a place with such a privileged location is so poorly managed. I had no choice but to book here because, due to circumstances, I looked at accommodations late, and there was only one room left. Therefore, I strongly recommend that anyone planning to spend a few days in Perhentian book well in advance to avoid the same experience we had. It would be a shame if what could be an unforgettable experience on paradise beaches were to become unforgettable for very different reasons.

The hotel itself is overpriced and they charge extortionate prices for essentials like water and coffee. A bottle of water costs 10MYR and a coffee 20MYR, while in George Town I paid just 2MYR for both. After sun in the shop is 39MYR, something you could get for less than half of that usually.

The bed was comfortable, the room was clean and the beach views were great. But I’d strongly recommend staying somewhere else and coming to this beach to visit.

textTranslated: We had a very pleasant stay at the Taaras, a hotel that particularly charmed us with its beautiful beach, the quality of its breakfast, and the kindness of its staff. We especially loved the breakfast restaurant team, who were very welcoming and attentive. We would also like to thank Nadia at reception, who provided excellent support throughout our stay. She was very efficient and available to answer all our questions, whether in person or via WhatsApp. The breakfast was excellent, with a special mention for the roti canai stand, which we thoroughly enjoyed. The hotel's beach is also magnificent, with crystal-clear blue water, making the setting particularly pleasant. However, we were surprised by certain aspects of the hotel. The value for money seemed disappointing, as the price was quite high for an establishment that appears somewhat dated and could benefit from several improvements, particularly regarding the bedding. This is the main drawback for a hotel of this category and price: we woke up in the morning with completely aching backs due to the poor quality of the mattress. We also regularly noticed sewer smells in the bathroom. Furthermore, we were surprised to have to pay for snorkeling masks and snorkels after only two hours of use. Given the hotel's price, this equipment should be provided free of charge, especially since guests come specifically to enjoy the hotel's beautiful beach. Overall, we had a very pleasant stay at the Taaras and particularly appreciated its exceptional setting, its beach, and the friendliness of its staff. The hotel is worth a visit, although some improvements would make the experience even more enjoyable.

text:
We stayed for three nights as a family of four and appreciated being upgraded to a larger two-bedroom Cliff Bay Suite. It was spacious and comfortable, and the complimentary minibar on arrival was a nice touch.

The resort’s greatest strength is undoubtedly its setting: a truly beautiful beach, clear water and a sheltered bay. Snorkelling with turtles was one of the highlights of our stay. We also paid to visit the turtle conservation centre, where our children learned about conservation and, under close supervision, carefully helped uncover baby turtles from the sand. It was a meaningful and memorable experience.

The complimentary entertainment lounge—with foosball, pool, table tennis, mahjong and carrom—was another good feature for families. Some staff were genuinely warm, friendly and full of smiles, particularly at ASEAN All Day Dining. The breakfast buffet itself, however, had a surprisingly limited spread for a five-star resort.

Unfortunately, service elsewhere was inconsistent. Some buggy drivers appeared uninterested, and we observed one using his phone while driving, which was a genuine safety concern. Drinks ordered from the bar never arrived, while indoor dining involved long waits and follow-up calls. The repeated lapses across different departments suggested wider issues with training, supervision and internal communication rather than a single isolated incident.

Food and drinks were expensive, yet the quality and service did not consistently justify the prices. The excursions were also costly, although the turtle conservation visit was a worthwhile exception. The kids’ club felt basic and underwhelming for a family resort at this price point. While our upgraded suite was spacious, the room and several other areas felt dated and overdue for refurbishment.

We also found it odd that sustainability videos from 2020 were still being shown without more recent updates. Our conservation-centre visit showed that at least some valuable work continues, but relying on six-year-old material leaves guests wondering about the progress of the resort’s other initiatives. The beach and water remain beautiful, although they did not always appear quite as pristine as in the older footage.

The Taaras has the ingredients to be exceptional: an extraordinary beach, memorable wildlife experiences, spacious accommodation and clear international appeal, including among the many Italian visitors we encountered. However, a five-star experience must also include consistently attentive service, safe practices, well-maintained facilities, good food and value for money. On those measures, our stay felt closer to a four-star experience despite luxury-level prices.

As Malaysian guests, we genuinely wanted to support and recommend a local resort attracting visitors from around the world. That is why this was more disappointing than upsetting. With better training, coordination, maintenance and value, The Taaras could be outstanding. Based on our experience and the price paid, however, we would find it difficult to recommend it in its present form.

text:
We booked our stay through an agent at Perhentian Island Resort, which is already notably more expensive than other nearby hotels. Unfortunately, the arrival and check-in experience left much to be scenery.

Upon arriving at the jetty around 11:00 am, we were greeted with a complete lack of guidance or a proper welcome. There were no signs or staff directing us, so we had to walk blindly from the jetty to find the reception counter on our own.

Our travel agent's itinerary, noted that check-in could be as early as 12:00 pm (international check-in time). However, hotel staff told us we had to wait until 3:00 pm for our seaview chalet. We left our bags in the luggage room and wandered the beach to pass the time. Even after pushing our luck, the receptionist wouldn't hand over the keys until 2:00 pm.

The chalet was well air-conditioned, and basic amenities were provided for our 3-day stay. We were also very fortunate to have a continuous water supply despite receiving a letter about a potential water disruption.

The toilet had a bit of a smell. Additionally, the two power outlets next to the mirror were broken, forcing us to share the working plug with the kettle.

The provided mugs and glass cups were visibly dirty. We had to physically bring them back to reception to demand a clean replacement.

Also, make sure to pack plenty of insect repellent as the mosquitoes right outside the rooms are relentless!

The beach itself is absolutely gorgeous, clean, and crystal clear so no complaints there! You can easily spot baby blacktip reef sharks, stingrays, and schools of fish right by the shore.

Because this beach doubles as a major island snorkeling point, it gets quite noisy when all the tour boats park close to the sand. It is also incredibly frustrating to find an open beach chair to place your belongings, as families tend to hog and hoard them all day.

We had the full breakfast, lunch, and dinner buffet during our stay. The food definitely needs improvement. Many of the dishes didn't taste very good or were heavily over-salted. On top of that, there was a major issue with flies landing on the buffet spreads; even though the resort installed those little spinning fan tools to shoo them away, they weren't very effective.

The beach and natural marine life are breathtaking, but for the premium price tag, the resort desperately needs to step up its service, room maintenance, and buffet quality.

Un soggiorno davvero eccellente a Redang

The Taaras Beach & Spa Resort merita sicuramente una recensione molto positiva, a partire dall’ampiezza degli spazi, dalla pulizia generale della struttura e dalle dimensioni delle camere, spaziose, confortevoli e molto ben curate.

L’accoglienza è di primario livello, con una particolare attenzione verso gli ospiti che arrivano dopo un viaggio inevitabilmente stanchi e accaldati. Nel nostro caso, è stato di grandissimo supporto Bryan, che si è reso immediatamente disponibile ad assisterci per qualsiasi necessità durante il soggiorno. Una presenza discreta ma costante, con una comunicazione via WhatsApp sempre recepita e soprattutto tempestiva. Un servizio che abbiamo apprezzato moltissimo.

Anche la ristorazione è stata una piacevole sorpresa. La proposta non si limita alla cucina asiatica, ma offre anche diversi piatti internazionali di ottima qualità, accompagnati da una carta dei vini decisamente interessante. text:
The Verdict: Stay somewhere else and just visit this beach.
Perhentian Island Resort sits on what is arguably the most breathtaking, crystal-clear stretch of white sand and turtle-snorkeling reef on the entire island. However, the resort itself is a massive letdown. You are paying a premium price for a property that feels neglected, dated, and poorly managed.

The Bad: The rooms are in desperate need of a renovation—expect septic tank smell from poorly maintained toilets, musty smell, stained linens, plumbing issues, in room safe that does not work , and zero Wi-Fi or poor phone signal in the chalets. - we changed rooms and had the same issues. The included buffet breakfast is incredibly basic and lacks quality and cleanliness (flies on food) while the overall resort infrastructure struggled with basic utilities like running water. (We could not shower, flush, or wash hands at one point our stay). 2 rooms per chalet have very thin walls, so expect smelling and hearing your neighbour if they have a conversation, or smoke a cigarette.

The Good: The location is a 10/10. The water is pristine, and you can literally swim out from the shore to snorkel with sea turtles and fish without needing a boat tour.

Final Thoughts and recommendations: Do not look at the booking photos; they do not reflect the current run-down state of the rooms and common areas. Save yourself the frustration: book a better-maintained hotel nearby for a comfortable night's sleep, and just take a water taxi over to this beach during the day to enjoy the spectacular nature.

Recommend to upgrade at least on plumbing and ventilation infrastructures, and management to have goals to realise the full potential of this wonderful location.

text:
Yes, it is expensive for the quality offered, but it’s worth it! Best location on the island: we woke up everyday at 8:30/9am and ran to the sea to swim with turtles, all by ourselves! They can be found all around the day: morning, lunch, and late afternoon, we always saw them. In the morning, from the pier, you can see dark shadows in the water - that’s them. At around 10:30am the boats arrive with hundreds of tourists, so it’s best to catch them early. There’s all sorts of animal life in this resort: the cutest monkeys we’ve ever seen, lizards, bats, squirrels, etc. It’s like staying in an open zoo. Plus the beach is truly beautiful.
We stayed in the A-Frame rooms, private cabins with shared bathrooms, and honestly I think it’s even better than staying in the big houses (because they share a wall with neighbors). These cabins felt very private and had a nice seaview. Also, it’s less than half the price of the other options. The fan works wonders and no animals entered the room during the night (not even mosquitos). Shared bathrooms were very close by and clean.

However…the sheets didn’t look clean when we arrived (had hairs on them). But after a few days in Malaysia I’ve noticed the cleaning standards are pretty low. My partner got some weird bites on his skin - might have been bedbugs (we heard other guests who were staying in the big houses complaining of this too).

The breakfast buffet - just stick to fresh stuff and it’s good. Eggs, fruit, noodles and vegetables. The “western” options are all terrible, frozen and fried.

The restaurant is expensive (then again, Besar is more expensive than the mainland). Again, stick to local food and you’ll be fine. Most of the times we opted to eat in Mama’s, 15min walk from the resort. Cheapest prices on the island and good local food.

La baia privata è semplicemente spettacolare: acqua cristallina, sabbia bianca e un’atmosfera rilassante che rende questo luogo un vero paradiso. Lo yatch del proprietario onnipresente che rovina la vista, e nota negativa del personale che non ha occhio per tenere pulito dalla plastica e carta in spiaggia. Personale disponibile. L’unico piccolo appunto è che, a tratti, il servizio è sembrato un po’ “robotizzato”, molto formale e meno spontaneo rispetto ad altri resort che abbiamo visitato.

textTranslated:
We stayed a few nights at the Taaras Beach Resort and had a truly wonderful experience. We chose a Cliff Suite with an ocean view, and waking up every morning to such a view was priceless.

The private bay is simply spectacular: crystal-clear water, white sand, and a relaxing atmosphere that makes this place a true paradise. The owner's omnipresent yacht spoils the view, and the staff, who have no eye for keeping the beach clear of plastic and paper, are a downside. Everyone is careful about how to rescue and release baby turtles, but there's no need to worry about disposable items on the beach. The resort offers a wide range of activities, from kayaking to water sports, and a well-organized dive center for those who want to explore the magnificent seabed.

The dining options are also very comprehensive, with the option of choosing between buffets and à la carte restaurants without having to leave the resort. Since the entire island complex covers practically the entire island, you'll find everything you need.

Helpful staff. The only small complaint is that, at times, the service seemed a bit "robotized," very formal and less spontaneous than other resorts we've visited.

Overall, it's a destination we absolutely recommend to anyone seeking picture-perfect sea views, relaxation, diving, and comfort in an exclusive setting. A stay we'll remember fondly.

text:
Just returned home after a 4 night/5 day stay at the Taaras. This has been one of my favourite ever breaks.
Pros
Location - is extraordinary. A peaceful bay, beautiful beach and crystal clear water that you can wade out to for a long distance while still being able to stand - perfect for swimming/snorkelling with kids. Wake at 6.30 one morning if you can to experience the sunrise, is quite special.
Staff - every single person we interacted with was warm, friendly and wanted to help. Particular mentions for Saiful and Dino at Asean, Rizal (spelling?, sorry) at Cove and Hamdan in guest relations who were all so helpful, professional and kind. Again though, every single member of staff was great to interact with.
Rooms - we had a cliff bay suite and it had the nicest view of any room I've stayed in. Beds were extremely comfortable and aircon worked well.
I also liked the nice mix of guests from different parts of the world - no one group overwhelms the place as can sometimes be the case at other resorts.
Cons
It is a fairly remote location, so variety of food options is understandably less than on mainland, but they still do a good job and we always found something delicious at buffet time.
One tiny gripe from me - not selling bottled mineral water in the shop means paying a high price at one of the restaurants. This felt a little mean, but they do provide filtered water top ups when asked.

Overall, a wonderful place. We intend to return soon.

text:
For our recent getaway, we booked The Taaras, supposedly the best hotel on Redang Island. With that reputation and the price tag, we arrived expecting a little bit of wow.

Arrival:
The welcome was pretty much “hey you made it.”  . We were served a welcome drink that tasted as if the juice concentrate was more of a suggestion than an ingredient.

We arrived way too early and our room wasn’t ready for early check-in, so we were then told to leave our bags on the floor by the stairs. For a resort charging these rates, I assumed a proper luggage area might have made it into the budget, but apparently not- the staircase floor is the luggage lounge.

We left our bags to enjoy the beach, and we can confirm this is where The Taaras absolutely earns its reputation.

The beach:
The beach is breathtaking. Hands down, the most beautiful beach on Redang Island. The sand is incredibly white, the water is crystal clear, and the scenery is spectacular. If the welcome drink was 99% water and 1% juice, at least the water at the beach was actually impressive.

The room:
Our Bay View room was amazing. A big thank you to the hotel management for assigning us Room 251. The room was perfect, and the view of the beach was spectacular. We loved the slice of cake and the beautiful anniversary message displayed on the screen- though we had to turn on the TV to see it. It was a thoughtful touch.

Breakfast at Asian Dining restaurant:
Breakfast had a good spread, although most of the food sat comfortably in the moderately good category. The croissant was soft, and limp. The roti canai was fine, even though i think a splash of sambal would take it up a notch.

We ordered iced chocolate drinks, which arrived as a joke. Between this and the welcome drink, I strongly suspect the beverage department is either terrified of flavour or operating under extremely strict flavor rationing. Perhaps a little more training in beverage making?

Recreation Center:
We made good use of the Sports and Recreation Center. Renting equipment such as the canoes, snorkelling gear and an underwater camera was easy, and returning everything was straightforward. The staff were extremely helpful, especially Kak Husni, who made things simple for us

The only issue though was transferring the underwater camera files. We couldn’t transfer everything because the videos were large, despite averaging around two minutes each. If only the centre could temporarily upload the files to cloud storage and provide guests with a download link. That would save everyone from standing around watching a transfer progress bar move with the urgency of a sea cucumber.

Customer Service:
One thing that genuinely stood out was the customer service. The staff were consistently friendly and helpful, when approached, but some moments went beyond the usual resort service. A staff member helped attend to our minor wounds after a snorkelling activity, and we even saw another staff member helping a guest tie her hair. How lovely is that.

We had the pleasure of riding with Rafiq, one of the buggy drivers, who remembered us by our room number, so every trip between our room and the lobby was effortless. He shared helpful tips and was a pleasure to chat with.

Overall, The Taaras has an absolutely spectacular beach, beautiful views, excellent rooms and some genuinely wonderful staff. The natural setting does a lot of the heavy lifting.

They just have to work on the arrival experience, and beverage quality.

Abbiamo soggiornato al The Taaras Beach & Spa e, nel complesso, è stata un'esperienza molto positiva.

Il resort è bello, curato e rappresenta la migliore struttura dell'isola di Redang. Le Garden Suite sono ben tenute e, a mio parere, hanno una posizione decisamente più comoda rispetto alle camere vista mare, perché permettono di raggiungere facilmente spiaggia, piscina e ristoranti.

Il prezzo è sicuramente elevato rispetto a quanto viene offerto: personalmente lo considererei più vicino a un buon resort 4 stelle europeo che a un vero resort di lusso. Nonostante questo, resta comunque la scelta migliore sull'isola.

La colazione è ottima, molto varia e con ampia scelta. Il ristorante Asean, invece, non mi ha particolarmente convinta. Ho apprezzato il beach bar per la comodità e l'atmosfera, anche se la pizza è decisamente migliorabile. Suggerirei inoltre di ampliare le proposte vegetariane del ristorante the cove.

Il vero punto di forza è il servizio: ogni giorno lo staff contatta gli ospiti su WhatsApp per chiedere come sta andando il soggiorno ed è sempre rapido nel risolvere qualsiasi problema. Ho trovato molto piacevoli anche i piccoli dettagli, come i cioccolatini lasciati ogni sera in camera, il minibar rifornito quotidianamente, la lounge dedicata all'attesa all'aeroporto di Kuala Terengganu e la musica dal vivo durante l'aperitivo e la cena.

La pulizia è buona, la spiaggia è ben tenuta e la posizione è perfetta per raggiungere il punto di osservazione delle tartarughe. Lo snorkeling è molto bello, con la possibilità di noleggiare facilmente tutta l'attrezzatura necessaria. Un enorme valore aggiunto è poter assistere alla nidificazione delle tartarughe sulla spiaggia e, quando possibile, partecipare alla liberazione dei piccoli: un'esperienza davvero emozionante.

Ho trovato molto comodo anche avere il villaggio proprio accanto al resort, dove si può cenare nei ristoranti locali spendendo circa un terzo rispetto ai ristoranti dell'hotel e, spesso, mangiando anche meglio.

Il materasso è molto comodo, nella sala comune sono disponibili giochi per intrattenersi e il clima è stato perfetto: nonostante le previsioni indicassero pioggia continua, abbiamo avuto solo brevi acquazzoni notturni. Il mare è semplicemente il più caldo e azzurro che abbia mai visto e durante il soggiorno è possibile osservare tantissimi animali marini.

Ci sono però anche alcuni aspetti migliorabili. Le zanzare della sabbia sono numerosissime, anche all'interno delle camere: consiglio di portare un repellente davvero efficace. Alcune sdraio e tavolini sulla spiaggia avrebbero bisogno di una pulizia più accurata.

Non ho apprezzato la presenza costante dello yacht del proprietario ancorato nella baia, perché rovina un po' la vista naturale di questo luogo magnifico.

La nota più triste riguarda purtroppo la quantità di plastica e microplastiche presenti sia sulla spiaggia sia in mare. Il proprietario mostra con orgoglio i progetti di riqualificazione e pulizia, iniziativa davvero ammirevole, ma purtroppo basta fare pochi passi per trovare microplastiche, bottiglie, accendini e altri rifiuti. Mi sarebbe piaciuto trovare dei cestelli o dei sacchi messi a disposizione degli ospiti che desiderano dedicare un po' del loro tempo a ripulire questo paradiso.

Infine, avrei gradito un po' più di intrattenimento serale. A parte la piacevole musica dal vivo, le serate risultano piuttosto tranquille: una serata disco, un white party o qualche spettacolo aggiuntivo renderebbero l'esperienza ancora più completa.

Nel complesso consiglio il The Taaras Beach & Spa a chi cerca il mare più bello che si possa immaginare, un resort ben gestito e un servizio molto attento. Con qualche miglioramento e un rapporto qualità-prezzo più equilibrato potrebbe diventare davvero un punto di riferimento assoluto.
textTranslated:
We stayed at The Taaras Beach & Spa and, overall, it was a very positive experience.

The resort is beautiful, well-maintained, and is the best property on Redang Island. The Garden Suites are well-maintained and, in my opinion, are much more conveniently located than the sea-view rooms, as they allow easy access to the beach, pool, and restaurants.

The price is certainly high for what you get: personally, I'd consider it closer to a good European 4-star resort than a true luxury resort. Despite this, it's still the best choice on the island.

The breakfast is excellent, with a wide variety and selection. The Asean restaurant, on the other hand, didn't particularly impress me. I appreciated the beach bar for its convenience and atmosphere, although the pizza could definitely be improved. I would also suggest expanding the vegetarian options at The Cove restaurant.

The real strength is the service: the staff contacts guests daily via WhatsApp to ask how their stay is going and is always quick to resolve any issues. I also enjoyed the small details, such as the chocolates left in the room every evening, the daily restocked minibar, the dedicated airport lounge at Kuala Terengganu Airport, and the live music during aperitifs and dinner.

The cleanliness is excellent, the beach is well-maintained, and the location is perfect for reaching the turtle observation point. Snorkeling is excellent, with all the necessary equipment easily available for rent. A huge added bonus is being able to witness turtle nesting on the beach and, when possible, participate in the release of the hatchlings: a truly moving experience.

I also found it very convenient to have the village right next to the resort, where you can dine at local restaurants for about a third of the price of the hotel restaurants and, often, even better.

The mattress is very comfortable, there are games available in the common room for entertainment, and the weather was perfect: despite the forecast calling for continuous rain, we only had brief showers at night. The sea is simply the warmest and bluest I've ever seen, and during our stay, we were able to observe countless marine animals.

There are, however, some areas that could be improved. Sand mosquitoes are numerous, even inside the rooms: I recommend bringing a truly effective repellent. Some beach chairs and tables could use a more thorough cleaning.

I didn't appreciate the constant presence of the owner's yacht anchored in the bay, as it somewhat spoils the natural view of this magnificent place.

The saddest thing, unfortunately, is the amount of plastic and microplastics both on the beach and in the sea. The owner proudly displays the redevelopment and cleanup projects, a truly admirable initiative, but unfortunately, it only takes a few steps to find microplastics, bottles, lighters, and other waste. I would have liked to see bins or bags made available to guests who wish to dedicate some of their time to cleaning up this paradise.

Finally, I would have appreciated a little more evening entertainment. Aside from the pleasant live music, the evenings are quite relaxed: a disco, a white party, or some additional entertainment would make the experience even more complete.

Overall, I recommend The Taaras Beach & Spa to anyone looking for the most beautiful sea imaginable, a well-managed resort, and very attentive service. With a few improvements and a better quality-price ratio, it could truly become an absolute reference.

We stayed at The Taaras hoping for a relaxing family getaway, and while parts of it delivered, several avoidable issues took the shine off.

Room allocation: Before arriving, we specifically requested twin rooms in the same block, ideally close to reception, and were told this would be "accommodated." Despite the resort not being at full occupancy, we were placed in the garden view block furthest from reception — not the twins-together setup we'd asked for. Not the start we were hoping for.

Check-in: The check-in process itself felt underwhelming and rushed. We weren't given any orientation — no signage or directions to the beach, and no mention of the sandfly issue (more on that below) or the turtle release happening that same evening. We only found out about the turtle release from friendly staff down at the beach, and it ended up being a real highlight — but it shouldn't have been left to chance. It should also have been mentioned during check in that the hot water only works if you turn on the SWITCH for 15 minutes before taking a shower . as a result a poor cold first day shower experience with poor water pressure

Sandflies: This was our biggest issue. Nobody warned us about sandflies, and by the end of day one I'd been bitten around 25 times and my son closer to 50. The itching kept us both up most of the night. A simple heads-up at check-in (with repellent recommendations, or even repellent provided) would have made a huge difference.

Wifi: In-room wifi was patchy and unreliable throughout our stay.
The positives: The rooms themselves were genuinely luxurious and matched the price point. The beach is stunning — genuinely one of the best we've experienced — and the turtle release was a magical, unexpected bonus.

Spa: A real highlight of the trip. Glory's team massage was fantastic, and the traditional Taaras herbal bag massage was excellent — worth booking in advance. Glory herself was the first person we met who we could say embodied a true 5 star experience!

Staff: Mixed experience. The beach staff and spa team were warm and attentive. Reception, however, could use more training in guest service — better attention to pre-arrival requests and basic welcome information would go a long way, including information (and a basic leaflet for asking us to check amentiies via scannign a QR code - available we found AFTERWARDS)

In summary: Gorgeous location, excellent spa, but the resort needs to tighten up communication — from honoring room requests to warning guests about sandflies and letting them know about evening events like the turtle release.

Had a really pleasant stay at Berjaya Tioman Resort with my family. The resort is beautiful and our Beach Front Chalet had a lovely view. The shower was also surprisingly good — strong water pressure and easy to adjust the temperature, which made it very satisfying after a day at the beach!

The buggy service was excellent too. Very fast and efficient, even late at night.

We also booked a private snorkeling trip for RM750 for our family of four, and it was definitely worth it. Our guide, Pak Ki, was very patient and followed our pace and timing. The coral and marine life around Tioman were beautiful. My husband and son did get stung by jellyfish, but thankfully it wasn't serious.

The resort staff were all very friendly and helpful. They genuinely tried their best to accommodate our requests. One small gesture that really stood out was when I needed Panadol early in the morning while the gift shop was still closed. One of the staff kindly gave me some from his personal supply. Such a simple gesture, but very thoughtful and much appreciated. ❤️

The only downside for us was that the resort gets very quiet after around 8pm. I understand Tioman is more of a relaxing destination, and the coral-filled beach may limit certain water activities, but it would be nice to have some simple evening entertainment such as live acoustic music, a movie by the beach, sunset sessions, beach BBQs or stargazing.

There also isn't much happening around the nearby village apart from exploring by motorbike and finding places to eat, so having more activities within the resort would definitely make the stay even better.

Overall, we really enjoyed our stay. Beautiful resort, great staff, good service and an amazing snorkeling experience. Would definitely come back! 🌴🌊

Newly renovated rooms are available in our higher categories, and upgrading works are ongoing across the resort. text:
A resort that is clearly in need of renovation

Berjaya Tioman Resort has, according to its own website, been around since 1985. That makes it 41 years old, and unfortunately, the age of the resort is also quite noticeable in some of the rooms.

Our room had an outdated and very firm bed, with the springs clearly noticeable. There were also quite a lot of ants in the room, as well as several issues with the finishing that, in our opinion, do not fit a hotel presenting itself as a luxury golf resort. The door was sticking when both opening and closing. The wooden bathroom door showed clear signs of wood rot and had been poorly repaired. Since there is no shower curtain, the door gets very wet after every shower, which certainly does not help. The sealant around the sink also looked very old and overdue for replacement.

The dining experience also felt rather dated. The menus at the restaurant and bars are old-fashioned laminated, folded A4 sheets, and several items listed on them were simply not available, including drinks such as Hoegaarden, Corona and Piña Colada. There is also very little communication about which restaurants and bars are open and when. For a resort of this size and standard, we would expect both the menus and the communication about the available dining options to be kept more up to date.

We also found that quite a lot of staff members were travelling back and forth around the resort on scooters. Given the size of the property, this is perhaps understandable, but it does take away somewhat from the peaceful resort atmosphere you might expect from a place like this.

Berjaya Tioman Resort proudly presents itself as the largest resort on Tioman. We are aware that the resort is currently undergoing renovations and that some room categories have already been updated. However, this does not fully address the issue from a guest's perspective. At present, it seems to be a matter of luck whether you receive a renovated room or one that is clearly in need of updating, while paying the same price. Until the renovation is completed across the resort, the experience can therefore vary considerably depending on the room you are allocated.

In our view, the remaining rooms should be brought up to current standards, with more consistency across the resort in terms of both room quality and overall presentation.

Fortunately, there are also positive aspects. The activities on offer are well organised, and the lobby staff are incredibly friendly, helpful and accommodating. When we arrived, we were initially given a room with two single beds, even though we had booked a double bed. After we raised this, it was resolved quickly and without any hassle.

In short: a beautifully located resort with friendly staff and well-organised activities, but the condition of some of the rooms and the dated overall presentation unfortunately seriously detract from the overall experience. A thorough renovation and update would certainly be worthwhile.

textTranslated:
The beach is beautiful, and there's a boat dock within walking distance with about 50 baby sharks and thousands of fish. The food is good, and the buffet is plentiful. However, many items on the menu are unavailable; for example, there's only a small selection of wines and beers. They're clearly operating on a shoestring budget despite it being peak season.

You can book snorkeling tours, rent kayaks, and ride beach buggies.

Unfortunately, the resort is showing its age and gives the impression that they're no longer investing in it and are simply skimming profits. Only the restaurant and lobby look great; everything else is gradually falling apart. I can't understand the claim that renovations are being done in phases, because if barriers at the pool are broken or planks on bridges in the middle of the resort are sticking out into the walkway, these issues should be addressed immediately, not piecemeal.

The pool is okay, but not very inviting. The children's area is now without a slide and is dilapidated. Railings are broken and cordoned off with barrier tape. The pool bar is uninviting, just like the Sundown Bar, which really has potential. It's a real shame how carelessly it's managed, even though the staff are doing their best and are very friendly.

The golf course is beautifully situated. Since it's rarely played, it's in a correspondingly poor state, so maintenance isn't a priority. The clubhouse is like a derelict place; the rental clubs are from the 1980s and are mismatched sets.

The first nine holes were still enjoyable, even though the monkeys robbed me, and you have to walk (or drive) all the way back from the 9th tee because the bridge to the fairway is 3 meters short…

The rooms are okay, with everything you need, although the bathrooms are quite worn.

Just outside the resort gates, there's a very tasty Chinese restaurant by the sea that's also popular with locals. You can walk to the "city center" in 30 minutes or get a ride from Bob in his brightly lit tuk-tuk (he's at the scooter rental shop by the entrance, next to the barrier).

All in all, it was nice; the kids enjoyed it because they didn't "see" the points mentioned above.

What makes it particularly outrageous is the price. You are paying current resort prices for a property that looks decades behind in terms of maintenance and renovation.

text:
We had another wonderful experience at Kapalai Dive Resort. Our dive masters Ryan and Ardi were extremely friendly, knowledgeable, and excellent at spotting marine life. They were just as skilled at finding larger sea life as they were at discovering tiny macro creatures, which made every dive interesting. We saw a giant cuttlefish, a sleeping bamboo shark, and mimic octopi, amongst many other sea creatures! We had fantastic diving at Kapalai, Mabul, and the famous Sipadan Island, and really appreciated how attentive and experienced the dive team was.

The rest of the resort staff were also very friendly, welcoming, and helpful throughout our stay. The food was delicious and overall we felt the resort offered excellent value for such a unique experience.

One of the most fascinating things about Kapalai is the island itself. The tides completely change the scenery throughout the day. At high tide, the water can cover much of the island and you can have beautiful clear water directly underneath your chalet. At low tide, the water recedes, there may be little or no water beneath the chalet, and the exposed sand makes the island appear much larger. It was really interesting to watch the landscape transform with the tides.

Kapalai is a very special place and a fantastic choice for anyone who loves diving, marine life, and staying somewhere completely different from a typical resort. It's definitely worth the travel from Tawau airport. We would definitely recommend it!

Un cadre exceptionnel qui mériterait une expérience à la hauteur…

Nous avons séjourné au Sipadan Kapalai Dive Resort pour notre lune de miel, et le lieu est tout simplement incroyable. L’hôtel est magnifique, parfaitement intégré à son environnement, avec des chambres typiques pleines de charme.
Nous avions une chambre côté corail, que nous recommandons vivement : la vue sur l’océan est exceptionnelle et, le soir, les tortues viennent littéralement vous dire bonne nuit 🐢
La localisation est absolument superbe.
Une petite attention avait été préparée dans notre chambre pour notre lune de miel, avec une jolie décoration, ce qui nous a beaucoup touchés.
Le service est également irréprochable : le personnel est adorable, souriant, disponible et toujours très agréable.

🤿 Un énorme coup de cœur pour le dive center !
Mention spéciale au dive center, qui est pour nous l’un des gros points forts du séjour. Et surtout, un immense merci à Linda, notre instructrice, qui nous a permis de découvrir la plongée et de partir à la découverte de plusieurs très beaux spots. Grâce à elle, nous avons vécu une expérience vraiment inoubliable 🤿❤️

Sous l’eau, il y a énormément de choses à observer, avec notamment de très grandes tortues, et en quantité ! 🐢 C’est un véritable plaisir de les voir évoluer dans leur environnement naturel.
En revanche, il ne faut pas venir ici en s’attendant à découvrir une immense barrière de corail intacte. La richesse marine reste néanmoins très intéressante et les rencontres avec les tortues valent vraiment le détour.

🚨Les points qui nous ont déçus…
Le principal point négatif concerne malheureusement une partie de la clientèle, notamment les groupes de touristes chinois. Leur comportement a parfois réellement gâché le charme et la tranquillité du lieu : cris, manque de respect envers le personnel et les autres clients, et comportements qui nous ont semblé peu adaptés à un établissement de ce standing.
Nous avons également eu le sentiment que l’organisation du resort était très tourné vers cette clientèle.
C’est vraiment dommage, car un cadre aussi exceptionnel mériterait une ambiance beaucoup plus calme et respectueuse.
Nous trouvons notamment dommage que l’hôtel réserve directement une part importante de ses chambres à des agences chinoises. Cela semble contribuer à une forte concentration de cette clientèle au sein du resort et, par conséquent, à l’ambiance parfois très bruyante et peu respectueuse que nous avons pu constater pendant notre séjour.

🍽️ Le buffet, un autre point à améliorer…
Nous savons que nous sommes dans un resort all-inclusive 3 étoiles et nous n’attendions évidemment pas de la gastronomie. Mais avec des produits simples, il serait tout à fait possible de proposer une cuisine beaucoup plus qualitative.
Nous avons trouvé beaucoup de produits industriels, ce qui est dommage, et relativement peu de spécialités malaisiennes. C’est particulièrement regrettable lorsque l’on vient de l’étranger et que l’on souhaite justement découvrir la cuisine locale. Là encore, nous avons parfois eu l’impression que le buffet était davantage adapté aux habitudes de la clientèle chinoise qu’à une clientèle internationale.

📍En résumé :
Le Sipadan Kapalai Dive Resort pourrait vraiment avoir tout d’un 4 étoiles grâce à son cadre exceptionnel, ses chambres pleines de charme, sa localisation unique, la qualité de son personnel et surtout son excellent centre de plongée.
Malheureusement, certains choix concernant la clientèle accueillie et la restauration gâchent une partie de l’expérience et empêchent selon nous l’établissement d’être pleinement à la hauteur de son environnement exceptionnel.
Cela reste malgré tout un endroit magnifique et particulièrement adapté à une lune de miel. Dormir au milieu de l’océan, se réveiller avec cette vue et voir les tortues passer devant sa chambre est une expérience que nous n’oublierons pas ❤️🌴🐢🤿
textTranslated:
An exceptional setting that deserves an equally exceptional experience…

We stayed at the Sipadan Kapalai Dive Resort for our honeymoon, and the place is simply incredible. The hotel is magnificent, perfectly integrated into its surroundings, with charming, traditional rooms.
We had a coral-view room, which we highly recommend: the ocean view is breathtaking, and in the evening, the turtles literally come to say goodnight 🐢
The location is absolutely superb. A thoughtful touch had been prepared in our room for our honeymoon, with lovely decorations, which touched us deeply.

The service is also impeccable: the staff is lovely, smiling, helpful, and always very pleasant.

🤿 We absolutely loved the dive center!

Special mention goes to the dive center, which was one of the highlights of our stay. And above all, a huge thank you to Linda, our instructor, who introduced us to diving and took us to explore several beautiful dive sites. Thanks to her, we had a truly unforgettable experience 🤿❤️

Underwater, there's so much to see, including huge turtles, and lots of them! 🐢 It's a real pleasure to watch them in their natural environment.

However, don't come here expecting to find a vast, pristine coral reef. The marine life is still very interesting, and the encounters with the turtles are definitely worth the trip.

🚨The things that disappointed us…
The main negative point unfortunately concerns some of the clientele, particularly groups of Chinese tourists. Their behavior sometimes really spoiled the charm and tranquility of the place: shouting, disrespect towards the staff and other guests, and behavior that seemed inappropriate for an establishment of this caliber.

We also felt that the resort's organization was very geared towards this clientele.
It's a real shame, because such an exceptional setting deserves a much calmer and more respectful atmosphere.

We find it particularly regrettable that the hotel directly reserves a significant portion of its rooms for Chinese tour operators. This seems to contribute to a high concentration of this clientele within the resort and, consequently, to the sometimes very noisy and disrespectful atmosphere we experienced during our stay.

🍽️ The buffet, another area for improvement…
We know we're in a 3-star all-inclusive resort and we obviously weren't expecting haute cuisine. But with simple ingredients, it would be entirely possible to offer much higher-quality food.
We found a lot of processed foods, which is a shame, and relatively few Malaysian specialties. This is especially disappointing when you're coming from abroad and want to discover local cuisine. Again, we sometimes felt that the buffet was geared more towards the habits of Chinese guests than an international clientele.

📍In summary: The Sipadan Kapalai Dive Resort could truly be a 4-star establishment thanks to its exceptional setting, charming rooms, unique location, high-quality staff, and especially its excellent dive center.

Unfortunately, some choices regarding the clientele and the dining options detract from the experience and, in our opinion, prevent the resort from fully living up to its exceptional surroundings.

Nevertheless, it remains a magnificent place and particularly well-suited for a honeymoon. Sleeping in the middle of the ocean, waking up to this view, and watching turtles swim past your room is an experience we won't forget ❤️🌴🐢🤿

text: Before getting to the Taaras, we had heard so many great things about the place. Even ChatGPT says it’s considered *the country’s* highest end hotel. We thought that was the reason why we were asked to pay 400€ per night (2 people room). If you have never traveled to Malaysia, you might not be aware of the currency value, so just know that an average meal for 2 is worth 100MYR (20€). Therefore you can only imagine how expensive this hotel is. Now, for this kind of money you really do expect the best of the best. Unfortunately, as you might have guessed already, that’s not the case. This was quite literally the worst hotel we’ve stayed at since we landed in Malaysia. Besides the staff being very kind, although most of the times you feel the service doesn’t reach the luxury they promise, and the private beach being objectively beautiful, the rest is honestly terrible. The rooms are big, yes, but super dark and old - in fact, the furniture must have stayed the same since the resort opened in 1996. 2 out of the 3 restaurants available in the resort are quite bad both aesthetically and food wise. The Italian/Indian one is ok, but we spent 450MYR (90€) for 2 mains and 1 plate of fruit, so also not great. The pool is always dirty and infested by kids. The resort also offers “complimentary” activities - too bad we wanted to rent gear for SUP and they answered it was already taken - wasn’t aware 5 star hotels only owned 1 paddle surf. We also spent 180MYR (40€) for a snorkeling activity, which was basically right beside the beach, so we could have just swum to the snorkeling location, and without the other 15 people that were with us. As mentioned, the beach is really nice, white sands, pristine water - all great. Too bad the sun beds are as decadent as the rest of the resort, plus there’s a big unbalance between the number of beds and the amount of guests the complex can host. Overall, a terrible experience very much misaligned with the price you pay.

I stayed for 6 days.

Good points:
- The sea is beautiful.
However, having seen beautiful seas all over the world, I'd rate it about 7.5 out of 10. The beauty of the sea varies greatly depending on the weather and sea conditions.
- Abundant fish.

- Mostly Chinese tourists. They have bad manners.
The meals are buffet style, but they don't follow the rules. They don't line up and cut in from the side.
They don't consider the people after them, taking large quantities of anything that looks delicious, and when you come back later, there's nothing left. They create a hyena-like situation.
30 minutes after the meal starts, there's no delicious food left.
- The food is neither delicious nor bad.
The food isn't good considering the price.
Only the salad, fruit, and porridge are tasty.
Crab is sometimes served, but it has a rubbery texture.
- Everything is expensive.
Even renting a bicycle is expensive. If your cottage is far from the dining hall, it takes 7 to 10 minutes to walk there.
Alcohol is also expensive.
Only divers can go to Sipadan Island.
If you want to go snorkeling, you need to book an external tour. However, even the cheapest external tours cost 800 RM per person (approximately 32,000 yen per person).
Even divers have to pay an additional 450 RM to go to Sipadan Island.
In summary: The price and experience are not worth it.
You can have fun much more cheaply elsewhere.
If you are a diver and dive with a buddy the whole time, it might be cheaper.

This proves their commitment to best customer service and 5-star treatment. The food and drinks are a little pricey compare to KL standard. I guess they can charge that kind of price because there are not many options near the resort. They are pricey but they are very delicious. I saw some reviews that the food at the restaurant were not good. I disagree. There are three restaurants at the resort and I've tried all of them. Everything that I ordered from those restaurants are delicious with beautiful presentations. If you want something cheaper, there are a few seafood restaurants in short walking distance.

Let me tell you what's unique about this resort:
1. The location of the resort is the best. It's right on the bay which means the beach is private to the resort. The beach is quiet, calm, very clean, beautiful sand and pristine water. You feel like you're on a private beach all to yourself. The turtle snorkeling spot is super close, so you can rent a kayak from the resort and kayak to the turtle point and snorkel with the turtles up close.

2. The resort has it's own private airline - the Berjaya Air. If you're a tourist like me and time is super precious, do spend the money to take the Berjaya Air from Subang KL airport. The extra $$ is so worth it, you get the VIP experience and saves so much time. I arrived to the airport 1 hour before flight, Grab from KL to Subang was about 20 mins, flight duration was 1 hour that flew me directly into the island's airport which is 5 mins drive to the resort.  Imagine getting to the resort in less than 2.5 hours from KL?! The flight is pricey because it is a charter flight, new and super nice ATR-72 plane, single seater, (26 seats on the plane), meal was included, VIP lounge before flight also included breakfast and snacks.

3. The resort's staff workers. Everyone was so genuinely nice, friendly and helpful. Kudos to the customer service team, front desk, restaurant servers, recreation center, buggy drivers, housekeeping ladies.

If you're looking for a relaxed and calm atmosphere resort with beautiful calm beach and excellent scenery, the resort is for you. There are no loud music, big annoying crowds or party people.
We stayed three nights, 1st day chilled at the beach and pool, 2nd day snorkeling and island hopping and 3rd day last chill at the beach and pool. Perfect relaxing vacation after busy time at KL.

🛏️ Room
Our room was spacious and clean, providing a comfortable stay overall. There were a couple of minor issues during our stay, including a short circuit and a problem with the safe, but both were rectified promptly and smoothly by the staff, which we appreciated.
The balcony, however, appears a bit aged and the railing feels somewhat fragile (there is a warning sign advising guests not to lean on it). It would be good if the hotel could refurbish or better maintain this area to enhance safety and overall experience.

🍽️ Food
The all-day ASEAN dining restaurant offered reasonably good food. While the selection is somewhat limited, we appreciated that the menu changes daily, which adds some variety.
The Cove restaurant was more average in both taste and value, especially considering the pricing, which could be improved to better match expectations.

🎯 Facilities & Overall Experience
The resort is very family-friendly, with a wide range of activities suitable for both kids and adults. A highlight for us was the indoor kids’ room, where children can enjoy the trampoline, ball pit, and slide, along with some additional paid activities to keep them engaged.
The buggy service was quick and efficient, making it easy to get around the resort, especially between the room and the lobby.
The staff were consistently friendly, attentive, and proactive, always ready to provide helpful suggestions when needed. We would also like to give a special appreciation to our Guest Experience Executive, Hamdam Rajab, who took great care of us and made our stay even more pleasant.
The resort features a private beach accessible only to guests, making it feel safe, exclusive, and not overcrowded. The beach itself is clean, calm, and very enjoyable — definitely one of the highlights of the stay.
One area for improvement would be the swimming pool, which is relatively small and looks a bit dated. However, this was not a major drawback for us since the beach is just nearby and serves as a better alternative. The pool feels more like a complementary feature rather than the main attraction.

✅ Overall
A great resort for a relaxing family getaway, with excellent service, kid-friendly facilities, and a beautiful private beachfront — with some minor room and facility improvements that could further enhance the experience.

text:
I recently spent 3 nights at Sipadan Kapalai Dive Resort, and unfortunately, it was a major disappointment. While the location is naturally beautiful, the resort’s management and operations are overwhelmingly biased toward a specific demographic, leaving international travelers in the dark and ignoring basic environmental ethics.
Communication & Service Gaps
The resort feels entirely geared toward mainland Chinese tourists, to the point where English-speaking guests are treated as an afterthought.
• The Briefing: Our "welcome briefing" in English lasted a mere 2 minutes and lacked vital information. Meanwhile, the Chinese-language briefing went on for 20 minutes. We missed out on key details, such as the option to visit neighboring islands to purchase fresh seafood to bring back.
• Logistics: Announcements are a struggle. When calling room numbers for boat departures or activities, staff used Chinese numbers only. Despite my name being clearly English on the manifest, I had to guess when they were referring to me.
• Payments: Even the bar is restrictive. They  accept QR code payments designed for mainland Chinese users, no acceptance of international credit cards or cash.
Environmental & Diving Concerns
This was the most upsetting part of the stay. For a resort located in such a delicate marine ecosystem, the lack of oversight is appalling.
• Wildlife Harassment: I witnessed guests (specifically from the majority group) petting and harassing sea turtles. Despite reporting this to the staff multiple times, zero action was taken.
• Poor Diving Standards: Many of the divers currently visiting appear to be unqualified or poorly trained. I saw constant reef damage—divers kicking the coral, touching marine life, and poking animals for photos.
• Staff Negligence: The dive guides and resort staff seem to prioritize guest "satisfaction" (allowing them to do whatever they want) over the protection of the reef.
Final Verdict
If you are an English speaker or a diver who cares about marine conservation and reef etiquette, stay elsewhere. The blatant disregard for environmental rules and the massive language barrier in service makes this resort a poor choice for global travelers. There are far better options in the Semporna area that respect both their guests and the ocean.

text:
This is my first time staying at Berjaya Tioman Resort. I have been to Tioman Island numerous times, and always thought Berjaya Tioman Resort is such a high-end resort at Tioman island, and the resort must be of very high quality. However, after the stay at Berjaya, my impression had changed drastically.

The room condition is generally acceptable. The room comes with all the basic necessities. But, when we checked in, to our surprise, toilet roll was not provided! We had to ask for it. That is just tip of the iceberg. Then, here came the housekeeping with 1 roll of toilet roll! My friend was even joking, 'that's very generous of Berjaya"! The property is huge. There is buggy service to move guests around. But, the waiting time for the buggy pick-up is ridiculously long! On average, a 20 to 30 min waiting time is needed. Third time, again we waited at the Main Gate for >20 mins for buggy under the hot sun (luckily the security guard offered us their chairs to sit)

Berjaya has always known to be prestigious name in the industry, but Berjaya Tioman is far from a 4-star certified hotel. I would choose the budget homestay at Kampung Tekek over Berjaya considering the amount of money I had paid for the room!

潛水係最大亮點。Kapalai 附近潛點微距生物非常多，潛導專業又有耐性，會細心帶你睇生物，就算唔係資深潛水員都覺得安心同享受。整體安排唔趕，節奏好舒服。

餐飲選擇唔算多，但食物新鮮，潛水完食會特別滿足。
整體嚟講，呢度唔適合想玩樂或夜生活嘅人，但如果你係為潛水同真正放鬆而嚟，Kapalai 係一個好值得體驗嘅地方。

English

Staying at Sipadan Kapalai Dive Resort truly felt like disconnecting from everyday life. The resort is built over the sea, surrounded by water in every direction, with a very peaceful atmosphere. Sunrises and sunsets are beautiful, and at night you only hear the sound of the ocean — perfect for relaxing and relieving stress.

Diving is definitely the highlight. The nearby dive sites around Kapalai are rich in macro marine life, and the dive guides are professional and patient, always taking time to point out small creatures. Even for non-expert divers, the experience feels safe and enjoyable. The schedule is well-paced and not rushed.

The water villas are simple but comfortable, clean, with good air conditioning and comfortable beds. WiFi is limited, but that actually helps you unplug and fully relax.

Food options are not extensive, but meals are fresh and satisfying, especially after diving.
Overall, this is not a resort for nightlife or entertainment, but if you come for diving and true relaxation, Sipadan Kapalai is absolutely worth it.
