The location is truly a gem — the bay is stunning, the beach remains one of the most beautiful in Malaysia, and the staff are exceptionally friendly and welcoming. We will definitely return again.

That said, there are a few areas that deserve attention and improvement.

The general condition of the resort shows signs of aging and a major renovation is becoming necessary. The old roofing with visible discoloration gives parts of the resort an outdated feeling. The pool area also needs refurbishment, especially the bridge near the pool, which looks worn and old. A general revamp would greatly elevate the overall luxury experience.

The location alone cannot guarantee long-term success if maintenance and modernization are not prioritized. Considering the room rates range between RM2,500 and RM4,500 per night — making Taaras one of the most expensive resorts in Malaysia — guest expectations are naturally very high.

For these prices, I expected more attention to detail, especially regarding food and beverage quality. Breakfast should include genuinely fresh-squeezed orange juice, not artificial juice labeled as “fresh.” Small upgrades can make a huge difference in perceived luxury. Offering Prosecco at breakfast, as commonly found in many European 5-star hotels, would also elevate the experience significantly. If the resort wants to compete in the “Champions League” of luxury hospitality, serving cordial drinks at breakfast should be reconsidered.

I would give this hotel 0 stars if I could. Do not waste your time and money going here.

We booked a cliff suite for two nights. I’ll start with the positives - the view is nice and the water is blue and clear. The staff are friendly.

Now for the negatives:

We arrived to a chaotic reception and waited for a few hours for our room (257) to be ready. After we were told by the reception desk that our room wasn’t ready we gathered our belongings in the reception where we were immediately pounced on by the spa manager who handed each of us a treatment menu and stood over us while we looked at it. After we declined, we waited on sun loungers on the beach. There is a buzzer to the bar to order drinks - we buzzed and someone came after about 20 minutes. No urgency, definitely no luxury. Sitting by the pool wasn’t an option as there wasn’t anywhere inviting to sit. Even if there was, the loungers face into the main hotel restaurant (why?) and the pool is not nice to look at.

When our room was ready we went back through to reception - which was still chaotic and loud - we were loaded onto a buggy with other families and taken to our room. It felt more like a cattle lorry than a 5* resort buggy. The reception staff also informed us that we would need to turn on the hot water 10-15 minutes before using the shower, which was surprising for a resort of this alleged ‘quality’.

Upon entering our room we were hit by a really foul smell. There were hairs on the floor and in the sink, and stains on the pillows and bed sheets. We told the reception desk that we were going for lunch and requested that housekeeping return to the room.

We ate lunch at the Asean restaurant. We both ordered king prawn fried rice which arrived without the prawns and was clearly cooked in dirty old oil. This cost £25. We didn’t return. There were screens all around the restaurant and in reception advertising activities turtle hatching (which wasn’t really what I wanted to watch while eating) - very tacky.

We went back to our room which had been re-cleaned but still had a foul smell. Everything looks tired and dirty. We saw monkeys riffling through (clean) bed sheets and towels, so it’s no wonder. Our towels had brown marks on them and need replacing desperately. The water pressure in the room was terrible, and the air con units urgently require replacing (along with everything else). It’s hard to articulate but it really just felt like a budget hotel.

At this stage we informed the front desk that we would be checking out the following morning and we made new travel arrangements. They offered to upgrade our room but we had seen enough (I think we had booked the most superior room type anyway) so politely declined. We ate dinner at a restaurant just outside the resort called Aima Grill Fish Restaurant (unconnected to the hotel) which was far better than the food we ate at lunchtime. We skipped breakfast and left the next morning. We have never left a hotel early before. They offered to refund the second night - I’ll update this review if the refund doesn’t end up materialising.

Although the view from our room was nice, having been on the beach we had seen quite a lot of rubbish both in the sand and the sea. In particular we noticed that the staff who stand near the towel counter leave their cigarette butts in the sand (when there is a bin close by) which explains why they are all over the beach. There is also a problem with sand flies - other people were covered in bites and there were notices about the sand flies on the beach and in our room.

Everything is either old, tired, broken or a combination of these things. I’m not entirely sure where the money is spent (our 2N stay cost nearly RM5800) but it is most certainly not on the hotel, hygiene or the guest experience. It is so gross.

At best this is a 2* resort masquerading as a luxury hotel. It is a complete rip off and we will never return or recommend it to anyone.

Les infrastructures sportives donnent l’impression d’être progressivement abandonnées. Même des activités simples comme le ping-pong sont facturées, ce qui est assez surprenant pour un resort.

Le restaurant propose des tarifs plus chers et moins raisonnables par rapport au coût de la vie en Malaisie. Le service montre rapidement ses limites : dès qu’il y a plus de trois ou quatre commandes en même temps, l’attente s’allonge considérablement. Nous avions un bungalow avec une magnifique vue sur la mer, ce qui est un vrai point fort. En revanche, l’intérieur mériterait une rénovation, notamment la salle de bain, dont la baignoire semblait dater d’une autre époque. C’est d’autant plus regrettable que d’autres chalets, visiblement plus modernes et mieux entretenus, étaient fermés durant notre séjour.

Heureusement, le cadre naturel rattrape en grande partie ces défauts. La mer est magnifique, la plage est superbe et très agréable, offrant un environnement idéal pour se détendre.
Avec un meilleur entretien des installations et une modernisation des hébergements, ce resort pourrait retrouver tout son potentiel.

The resort is an establishment that has undoubtedly seen some very good years, but today it suffers from a visible lack of maintenance. We had a bungalow with a magnificent sea view, which is a real plus. However, the interior is in need of renovation, especially the bathroom, whose bathtub seemed to be from another era. This is all the more regrettable since other chalets, visibly more modern and better maintained, were closed during our stay.

Fortunately, the natural setting largely makes up for these shortcomings. The sea is magnificent, the beach is superb and very pleasant, offering an ideal environment for relaxation.

With better maintenance of the facilities and modernization of the accommodations, this resort could regain its full potential.

⚠️ Outside the resort, there's a restaurant just as expensive as the one inside! Stick to the one inside the resort…

text:
The resort is set in a huge bay within the island and you have access to their private beach and clear sea water.  There are lots of resort activities you can do at a cost.  All rooms get 1 hour of kayaking per stay, per occupant.

There is a very wide range of room types, that are set in villas and complexes, which are located from the beach front right up into the hills overlooking the bay.  However, be aware that the most private rooms are in fact one of their cheapest offerings.  The garden suites, and if you want the most privacy possible, as for an upper level suite in a corner / end of row unit, away from heavy foot traffic.  To be honest and having stayed in many luxury resorts, I would say that this place is a little over priced, but there isn't a better resort on the island, so you are basically paying for their exclusivity, which they can charge as they deem fit as there's no direct competitor.

The staff were amazing, always willing to help with your needs and unlike many other hotels and resorts, they respond to any issues very promptly. You get assigned a personal concierge, who is but phone call or WhatsApp text away.

The restaurant food is quite pricey and overall reviews are average, but the convenience is still good.  There are plenty of good restaurants in the local area within a 10 minute walk and there is a supermarket , stocking all your essentials.

This is a child friendly resort and I saw lots of families here with young children.

I would highly recommend renting your own vehicle when coming from the mainland and you can leave it for a small fee at a car park on the Merang waterfront jetty. Driving in Malaysia is not as challenging as you may think, especially if coming from the UK, as they drive on the same side.

Kapalai Resort, Sempona, Sabah, Malaysia

My friends and I stayed at Kapalai Resort for 4D3N in Dec 2023. The resort is entirely built on coral reefs and the accommodation is individual wooden chalet with ample privacy. I had a total of 9 dives around Mabul and Kapalai islands with 2 dives at nearby Sipadan island. Our best dives were at Sipadan Island where we saw tons of marine lives and a large school of Jacks. Snorkeling around Kapalai resort is accessible to many marine lives including the Hawksbill sea turtle. Sunset and sunrise were magnificent sights from the resort which provide great opportunity for photos shoot. The staffs on the resort are friendly and helpful and the amenities are adequate. However you may want to bring your own alcoholic drinks and snacks if you want to save some money. Meals are provided on the resort but limited to local dishes. However you have a choice to purchase seafood from the nearby Mabul island and the kitchen on the resort will be happy to cook them for  a small charge. We initially had a group of 4 but two of our friends had to cancel at the last minute due to medical and family emergencies. Kapalai resort could not offer a full refund but instead offered a change of date within 12 months from the initial date. Reason for rating 3 stars for service is because our booking was made through Kapalai Resort's agent Asia Dive Holidays (ADH) in KK and when we tried to reach ADH on WhatsApp to inform them of the emergency cancellation and refund, they were non-responsive and offered no assitance to us. We would not recommend Asia Dive Holidays for anyone looking at going to Kapalai resort or surrounding islands. We would also like Kapalai resort to review their partnership with Asia Dive Holidays and address the concerns we have regarding their unprofessionalism attitude and lousy customer service we received in our booking.

text:
Unfortunately, this was one of the most disappointing marine parks I’ve visited. We came here for snorkeling and an introductory dive expecting a beautiful, protected marine environment, but instead, large parts of the experience genuinely felt like swimming in a landfill.

There was an unbelievable amount of plastic and other waste both in the water and along the beach. While swimming, it was almost impossible not to encounter plastic bottles, bags, and other pieces of trash, sometimes even getting caught in your hair. I understand that currents can bring large amounts of waste into the area and that this is not necessarily something the park can prevent. However, what I cannot understand is how there seems to be so little organized effort to regularly remove it, especially from a place designated as a marine park and visited by tour boats every day. Everyone behaved as if this were completely normal and simply an everyday occurrence.

A French tourist family eventually took it upon themselves to start cleaning the beach and filled what looked like around 30 baskets with garbage. Seeing visitors taking responsibility for cleaning a marine park while people working there (mostly tour guides/divers)
carried on as normal was honestly quite shocking.

As for the marine life, we did see plenty of fish, which was nice, but unfortunately, most of the coral appeared to be dead or severely damaged. Considering this is a protected marine park, I expected a much healthier and more vibrant underwater ecosystem.

I really hope more is done to protect and maintain this place. If currents regularly bring this much waste here, then regular cleanups, collecting floating waste with nets, and better coordination with the tour operators visiting every day seem desperately needed. A marine park should be a place where marine ecosystems are actively protected, not somewhere visitors have to swim through plastic waste.

It was genuinely sad to see.

"3D CVzion merujuk kepada gabungan konsep Computer Vision dengan elemen visualisasi tiga dimensi (3D) yang digunakan bagi menghasilkan persekitaran maya yang lebih realistik dan interaktif. Dalam konteks kajian Pemvisualan Kreatif Marin Laut menerusi Animasi 3D, 3D -CVzion berfungsi sebagai pendekatan kreatif untuk menterjemahkan data marin, seperti bentuk terumbu karang, spesies ikan, serta suasana dasar laut, ke dalam bentuk animasi yang lebih meyakinkan dan mudah difahami oleh khalayak.Subjek dan rujukan visual dalam kajian ini diperoleh secara langsung melalui aktiviti selaman di Pulau Payar. Melalui teknologi ini, pengalaman visual dapat ditingkatkan kerana penonton bukan sahaja melihat bentuk dan warna, tetapi juga dapat membayangkan kedalaman, perspektif, serta gerakan yang hampir menyerupai keadaan sebenar di bawah laut."

1.Buka kamera telefon pintar anda dan imbas kod QR yang disediakan.

The subjects and visual references in this study were obtained directly through diving activities in Pulau Payar. Through this technology, the visual experience can be enhanced because the viewer not only sees shapes and colors, but can also imagine depth, perspective, and movement that closely resembles the actual conditions under the sea."

text:
We had a great experience at Pulau Payar. I was a little hesitant to go because I couldn’t find a lot of recent reviews. But I’m glad we booked a trip here. I imagine it’s a much better experience now that they limit the number of visitors per day to 100. That being the case, you need to book ahead of time to make sure you get a spot. (Bookings open around 1 month prior to scheduled visit.)

We did the “Intro Dive” package, which includes an assisted 30 minute scuba dive, limited depth, followed by snorkeling. As we had never scuba dived before (and had no certification), this was perfect for us to try out scuba. We really enjoyed it and have a good idea now if we want to pursue certification or not. A master diver will stay with you the whole time. After the dive, we were able to snorkel the rest of the time. I found the visibility to be pretty good and there were some nice coral formations and a good variety of fish. We saw a lot of colorful fish (parrot fish and others), some squid, an eel, and a few puffer fish (some really big ones too!) to name a few highlights.

Our day looked like this:
Met at the Scuba Club at 8:30am to register, try on gear, etc. Got on the boat a little after 9am and took the 1 hr-long, fast, bumpy, wet ride to Pulau Payar. Because we were doing the intro dive, we were on a boat with other scuba divers, while another boat took snorkelers only. So I can’t really comment on what the snorkelers in the other boat did. We went to a site off of the main island and did our dive. Then we snorkeled around while the others continued their dives. We had lunch on the boat (simple chicken and rice dish), then went to another site. After the divers got off the boat in deeper water, then boat took us to the shallower water for us to snorkel. There was a beach there also where we could relax. But most of the time we stayed in the water. After an hour or so, we got back on the boat and headed back to Langkawi. We arrived back, changed clothes and turned in our wet suits.

There’s limited places to change clothes. Either you have to use a small bathroom or a storage closet area. But it’s essential you change into dry clothes if you’re looking to take a Grab from there. In fact, they told us to walk away from the Scuba Club a little ways before ordering the Grab, otherwise they won’t pick you up because they assume you are wet.

Shout out to Hello Langkawi and staff members Maui (Aoi) and Nasi. They took good care of us.

text: The location and setting of this hotel is wonderful as it is all over the sea and a long way from land. The water is clear and shallow and there is loads of sea life all around so it’s like one big aquarium all the time. Unfortunately that’s where the good news ends, the hotel is dated and needs some updating and repair. The shower does not have hot water and there is a hot water switch is impossible to know whether it is on or off and you have to wait 15 minutes to get any hot water. Even then there is no guarantee that you will get any. There are no phones in the room so you need to call a landline number, which is the main office on the resort to order a golf buggy to get transported to the main parts of the resort. A buggy is necessary as the distances are quite long and the Sun is very hot with no shade. The rooms are large so it is difficult to get them fully the air-conditioned, which is necessary as it’s very hot here. The food is for the Chinese which I understand makes up 80% of the guests. Even then it is not a good standard in my opinion. I went with Malaysian friends and they said the same and they love Chinese food. There is no entertainment other than diving or snorkelling sad the worry about snorkelling is that there are plenty of sea snakes. We saw eight over the two days and most of them are by the steps that go into the water. The staff said they are not dangerous, but it is still a concern as they are seriously poisonous. I would recommend this location to divers although I did not visit any of the dive sites but the people I spoke to said they were good. Other than that this place will not keep you entertained for more than a couple of days at most.

textTranslated: This resort is incredibly relaxing and allows you to truly unwind. The ocean view is absolutely priceless; we stayed for two days and saw the sea every single day – we never got tired of it! There were tons of sea turtles swimming around outside our room; I've never seen sea turtles so close before. There were also tons of stingrays. The room's internet signal was a bit unstable, so I had to buy a data card. The signal was stronger near the counter. There was no TV in the room, so it's really a place for a proper vacation and relaxation, not for using electronic gadgets!
title: Sipadan Kapalai Dive Resort

text:
海景很美 很放鬆
房間蠻大的，但冷氣很小一台，機型也比較老舊，基本上白天待在房間裡會覺得悶熱。
島上的消費都可以記在房號上掛帳，活動只有浮潛跟水肺。
另外有配合的半日遊行程，廣告布條上寫的是要報名請到櫃檯報房號，結果事實上是，你要自己加微信聯絡，並且只能支付現金或使用支付寶…一個人一場的費用是250令吉，無法掛帳也沒有其他的解決方案，如果要想要參加半日遊行程，記得多帶點現金來！！！

這裡沒有免費的WiFi ，想要網路的話要跟櫃檯購買，自己有購買當地網路的話，房間的訊號也會不太穩定。

進出有高爾夫球車接送，但你需要先有一台可以打電話的手機，房間裡是沒有電話的。如果沒有剛好遇到高爾夫球車經過你房門前，你就需要自己走出來最外面用餐

每間房間插座規格不一定，有些房間是馬來西亞當地標準插座，有些是國際插座🔌這就要碰碰運氣了。
textTranslated:
The sea view is beautiful and very relaxing.

The room is quite large, but the air conditioner is small and outdated, making it stuffy during the day.

All expenses on the island can be charged to your room number. Activities are limited to snorkeling and scuba diving.

There are also half-day tours available. The advertisement says to register at the front desk with your room number, but in reality, you have to contact them via WeChat, and payment is only accepted in cash or Alipay… The cost is RM250 per person, and there are no other solutions besides charging your room number. If you want to participate in the half-day tour, remember to bring plenty of cash!

There is no free Wi-Fi. You need to purchase internet access at the front desk. Even if you purchase local internet, the signal in the room may be unstable.

Golf carts are available for transportation, but you need a mobile phone that can make calls; there are no phones in the rooms. If you don't happen to encounter a golf cart passing by your room, you'll need to go outside to eat.

The socket type varies from room to room; some rooms have Malaysian standard sockets, while others have international sockets. It's a matter of luck.
title: Sipadan Kapalai Dive Resort

Thank you for staying with us and for taking the time to share your detailed feedback.

It is also wonderful to hear that you enjoyed the diving activities and that our diving team provided professional, patient, and attentive service. At the same time, we are sorry to learn that your dining experiences did not reflect the same level of hospitality. We understand how disappointing it can be when service falls short of expectations, particularly when it affects multiple occasions during your stay.

Providing warm, courteous, and attentive service across all areas of the resort is important to us. We appreciate you bringing these concerns to our attention, and your feedback has been shared with the restaurant management team for review and further improvement.

We are grateful for your balanced feedback, recognising both the positive aspects of your stay and the areas where we need to do better. Comments such as yours help us improve the overall guest experience.

text:
I had mixed feelings about my stay at Berjaya Tioman.

First, I would like to thank the front desk staff and buggy service team. They were friendly, welcoming, and always willing to help. They proactively informed us about the activities available at the resort, which made us feel valued as guests.

I would also like to compliment the diving team. The staff were professional, patient, and provided detailed explanations throughout the activities. Their friendliness and attention to detail made the diving experience enjoyable and comfortable, especially for guests who may be less experienced.

Unfortunately, the restaurant service was a completely different experience. The attitude of several restaurant staff members was disappointing. When we ordered lunch and coffee, the way they spoke to us came across as rude and lacking basic courtesy. What was more disappointing was that this was not a one-time incident. Throughout our four-day stay, neither my family nor I encountered friendly or pleasant service at the restaurant.

For a resort of this standard, guests should not have to feel uncomfortable when dining. I sincerely hope the management will look into this matter and provide better customer service training for the restaurant team. The friendliness of the front desk, buggy service, and diving staff deserves recognition, but the poor attitude at the restaurant significantly affected our overall experience.

text: 早上司机准时到酒店来接我们到卡帕莱的专用码头，这个码头就在龙门客栈附近，坐9:30的船去卡帕莱岛。一上岛接待人员讲解了注意事项，我们吃了午餐后13:30就拿到了房间钥匙。第一天的房间为54号，第二天又换到了82号，两个房间的风景都不错，相对来说我们更喜欢82号一些，在这里能看到无比绚烂的日落。岛上还辟有给员工和军人住的一块区域，我们清晨在水上运动中心看到的在游泳的一群血气方刚的小伙子就是那些军人。其实这里不是一个岛，但有露出水面的沙滩。我们朝海里看，真地看到了一条游动的水蛇，甚至晚上还看到有一条大蛇顺着水上运动中心的阶梯爬到平台上睡觉，于是明白了这里的水屋为啥不像马尔代夫有阶梯直接通到海里。这里浮潜只能在水上运动中心附近划出的一片区域，我们发现有三种不同的鱼群，但比我们在诗巴丹看到的Jack鱼风暴和狼鱼风暴还是规模小了些。第二天我们还与另外两位客人500马币包船去了附近的马布岛，参观了那里的民居，但要进入岛上最豪华的那个度假村还要每人再花50马币，我们没进去参观。离开卡帕莱那天坐的是11点的船，前台还送了每人一块三明治作为午餐。回到卡帕莱的专用码头后，随后就被车送去了机场，非常完美！
textTranslated: The driver arrived at the hotel on time in the morning to pick us up and take us to the private pier for Kapalai, which is near the Longmen Inn. We took the 9:30 AM boat to Kapalai Island. Upon arrival, the staff explained the important information, and after lunch, we received our room keys at 1:30 PM. Our room for the first day was number 54, and we were moved to number 82 for the second day. Both rooms had nice views, but we preferred number 82, as we could see a spectacular sunset from there. There's also an area on the island for staff and military personnel; the group of energetic young men we saw swimming at the water sports center in the morning were those soldiers. Actually, it's not an island, but there are beaches that extend above the water. Looking into the sea, we actually saw a swimming water snake, and even at night we saw a large snake climb up the steps of the water sports center to sleep on the platform. This explained why the water villas here don't have steps leading directly into the sea like in the Maldives. Snorkeling here is limited to a designated area near the water sports center. We spotted three different schools of fish, but they were smaller than the jackfish and wolffish storms we saw in Sipadan. The next day, we and two other guests chartered a boat to nearby Mabul Island for 500 MYR to visit some local houses. However, to enter the island's most luxurious resort, it cost an additional 50 MYR per person, so we didn't go in. We took the 11:00 AM boat on the day we left Kapalai, and the receptionist even gave each of us a sandwich for lunch. After returning to Kapalai's private jetty, we were then taken to the airport – perfect!

Dear Guest,

Thank you for staying with us and for taking the time to share your detailed feedback.

We are truly disappointed to learn that your experience did not meet your expectations. The issues you have highlighted regarding housekeeping presentation, cleanliness of public areas, pool conditions, beach maintenance, power interruptions, and food hygiene are concerning, and we appreciate you bringing them to our attention.

We regret that housekeeping carts and linen bags were left near your accommodation during your stay. This is not the standard of presentation we strive to maintain, particularly in guest areas intended for comfort and relaxation.

We are also sorry to hear about the discomfort caused by insect bites. As a tropical island resort surrounded by nature, insects can occasionally be present despite our ongoing pest control programme. Nevertheless, your feedback has been shared with the relevant team for further review and monitoring.

Your comments regarding the swimming pool, poolside facilities, and beach cleanliness have been noted. Maintaining these recreational areas is important to the overall guest experience, and we regret that your observations left a negative impression.

We also apologise for the inconvenience caused by the temporary power outages during your stay. While such interruptions are uncommon, we understand the disruption they can cause to a holiday experience.

text:
After much consideration, I would not recommend anyone to book with this resort. I regret to say that it is not worth the RM 600 - 700++ per night stay and definitely not up to the standards of a 4 star hotel.

When we arrived last weekend, housekeeping carts were left beside our chalets, upon calling the lobby I was told that housekeeping has some rooms to clean later on nearby there so they left them (??!)
I asked them to please remove them as there were now already two carts in front of our stairs and multiple plastic bags of dirty towels.

All of us that stayed there got really bad bites from bed bugs!! They have still not healed.

The swimming pool is green and dirty. I was told they clean it everyday at 8am but in the 4 days I stayed, nobody cleaned it. Even the tiles were green and full of algae. The pool bar is closed down and abandoned and full of bird poop.

The beach only has a few lounge chairs at the most end of the beach and surprisingly exactly that area is not being cleaned. When we saw one of the staff cleaning the other part of the beach (with no chairs and no people), we asked them to kindly also clean the lounging area since there were cigarette buds etc. everywhere. We did also pick up the trash (not ours) ourselves but tbh I expect that a resort would maintain this.

We had two power outages throughout the stay - about 30 minutes.

The breakfast was good for most of the stay except for one morning there was spoiled milk in the coffee machine and milk dispenser. The coffee machine was not cleaned properly (rinse mode). Instead the team just replaced the milk carton and made one run-through with the new milk 🤢

I booked the hotel as I loved my stay at Berjaya Langkawi (very well maintained) but am honestly so disappointed in this resort from the Berjaya brand. It was really not worth the money and the trouble.

textTranslated:
The location is beautiful, but that's about it.

1. Room - The room is large, but there's only a small air conditioner, making it too hot to stay in and causing constant sweating. There's also no signal; asking at the front desk only results in being told to "purchase internet." The toilet has no door or curtain, making it difficult for ordinary families, except couples, to stay in it together during shower time. There's also no TV.

2. The sea view is stunning, but the area for snorkeling for hotel guests is smaller than the area open to visitors. You'll have nowhere to swim after just one morning, completely wasting the beautiful sea view.

3. No signal or internet is really inconvenient. The room is far from the restaurant, making it impossible to call a taxi. Imagine walking nearly 500 meters in the scorching sun for 15-20 minutes without any shade.

4. No shelter. The entire resort is unprotected, even the walk from the office to the restaurant is unprotected. It's impossible to walk through in the rain.

5. Customer service is terrible. This price shouldn't be the level of customer service. The staff are basically indifferent, and you have to solve everything yourself.

6. Food. Nothing special, just enough to fill you up.

Such a beautiful view, it's a real waste. If you're looking for a sea view room, consider Mabul.

text: L’hotel è molto bello, ma un po’ datato, le camere sono pulite e il panorama è mozzafiato. Purtroppo il ristorante è di qualità veramente bassa e c’è poca scelta per vegetariani/vegani, per cui spesso ci sono le stesse cose del giorno/giorni prima. Il diving centre è ok, nulla di più. La nostra guida faceva dei briefing molto sbrigativi e poco informativi. Sott’acqua andava molto veloce e non si curava molto dei subacquei con lui. Per fortuna c’erano sempre due guide e il nostro gruppo era abbastanza omogeneo e con esperienza. Le immersioni a Sipadan sono bellissime, ma Mabul non è niente di che. Bisognerebbe sempre cercare di andare a Sipadan, ma giustamente danno la possibilità a tutti di andare quindi alternano l’una e l’altra. Lo snorkeling intorno al resort si può fare solo in aree circoscritte..||Il personale dell’hotel e del diving è stato sempre molto gentile e disponibile. ||In generale, la cura dell’ambiente ci è sembrata poco attenta, essendo un resort completamente sull’acqua, si dovrebbero evitare mozziconi in acqua e bottiglie di plastica lasciate al caso. Indicano che se si spreca cibo del buffet possono dare una sovrapprezzo, ma in pratica non controllava nessuno. E di cibo sprecato, purtroppo, ne abbiamo visto tanto. Il Wifi (a pagamento) è stato inutilizzabile perché non c’è campo, ma se avete un buon roaming funziona un po’ ovunque.
textTranslated: The hotel is very nice, but a little dated. The rooms are clean, and the view is breathtaking. Unfortunately, the restaurant is very poor quality and offers little vegetarian/vegan options, so you often get the same dishes as the day/days before. The diving center is okay, nothing more. Our guide gave very cursory and uninformative briefings. He went very fast underwater and didn't pay much attention to the other divers with him. Luckily, there were always two guides, and our group was fairly homogeneous and experienced. The diving in Sipadan is beautiful, but Mabul is nothing special. You should always try to go to Sipadan, but rightly so, they give everyone the opportunity to go, so they alternate between the two. Snorkeling around the resort is only allowed in restricted areas. The hotel and diving center staff were always very kind and helpful. Overall, we found the environmental protection lacking. Being a resort completely on the water, cigarette butts in the water and plastic bottles left lying around should be avoided. They indicate that if you waste buffet food, they can charge a surcharge, but in practice, no one checked. And unfortunately, we saw a lot of wasted food. The Wi-Fi (paid) was unusable because there's no signal, but if you have good roaming, it works pretty much everywhere.

text:
Overall Impression
Except for the view, everything else fell far below expectations. I paid nearly RM6,000 for 2 nights, but the stay was nowhere near worth the price. This is not a 5-star resort—it is closer to 3-star. The property relies solely on its location while neglecting service, facilities, and maintenance. Unfortunately, other guests have raised similar issues in past reviews, and it is clear that no real improvements have been made.

Ratings
•	Price/Value: 2/5
•	Scenery & Location: 4/5
•	Facilities: 2/5
•	Access: 2/5
•	Service Quality: 2/5
•	Dining: 1/5
•	Cleanliness: 3/5

Beach & Location
The white sand beach was beautiful, clean, and well maintained. The view from the Cliff Bayview Suite was stunning. On this point alone, the resort deserves 5/5.

Room & Facilities
The suite was poorly maintained: TVs did not work, the air conditioner was broken, the floors felt gritty, and the bed mattress was uncomfortably hard. Bathwater was yellowish and cloudy, and tap water had a strong unpleasant smell. In-room dining dishes were left in the hallway for over two days. The bathroom amenities (L’Occitane) had an overly strong, chemical scent.
There were also two large flies inside the room, which gave a very unclean.This did not feel like a 5-star resort.

Check-in / Check-out & Service
While early check-in was allowed, overall service was unfriendly and mechanical. The welcome drink was handed out carelessly. The check-in process was rushed, with no explanation of facilities or activities. At check-out, staff simply processed the paperwork with no smile, no feedback, and no hospitality.

Dining
Breakfast was poor: hot dishes were already cold, the selection was limited, and seasoning was extreme. Complimentary soft drinks were only high-sugar choices (Fanta, A&W, Coke). Overall, the food quality was closer to 3-star level.

Activities
The snorkeling tour was disappointing: many corals were bleached, fish variety was low, and the sea was overcrowded with tours from the nearby public beach.

Other Issues
Wi-Fi did not work. Hot water took over 15 minutes to arrive and quickly turned cold. Guests had to set up their own sun loungers and collect towels from the counter. No complimentary water was provided.

Access
The resort is difficult to reach: 1-hour flight from Kuala Lumpur to Kuala Terengganu, another 1-hour drive to the jetty, and then a 40-minute boat ride. For international travelers, it is a long journey with little reward.

Please do not respond with a generic template reply. What matters is genuine improvement. As long as repeated guest concerns remain unaddressed, this resort will continue to disappoint.

Berjaya Resort in Tioman is in a stunning location, with a lovely beach and peaceful surroundings that make it easy to unwind. The natural beauty of the island is definitely the highlight.

The pool area could use some refreshing too — the towels really need replacing, and the exterior of the pool looks quite tired and could do with a fresh coat of paint.

Dinner was a bit of a letdown compared to breakfast — it would be great to see more local dishes, especially fresh fish and crab, to really match the island experience.

There also seemed to be a lot of security around, which felt a bit unnecessary for such a relaxed island setting.

Overall, it’s a beautiful spot with great potential, and with a few improvements, it could be truly exceptional.

I know it’s tempting to snorkel with turtles, but what The Taaras is doing under the guise of “research” is deeply concerning. They feed the turtles pieces of squid to the point that their natural, plant-based diet is completely disrupted. On top of that, up to 20 boats with 15–20 guests each were anchored at the turtle spot at the same time— it felt more like a chaotic wrestling match with other tourists kicking the turtles and other guests, than a peaceful or respectful experience for either guests or turtles. It’s nothing more than a money-making machine.

The same goes for their so-called “Hatching” event, where guests can buy the chance to release a baby turtle. With loudspeakers blasting, around 50 guests lined up and many mishandled the hatchlings — some even dropped them or squeezed them — while the “biologist” provided little explanation or guidance. This is not responsible conservation, nor is it species-appropriate handling.

Absolutely disgraceful.

Lasciatemi in questo paradiso!

L’hotel gode di una posizione spettacolare, immerso nella natura e affacciato direttamente sulla baia di Redang, un vero angolo di mondo che sembra dipinto. Abbiamo soggiornato in una suite Cliff Bay, prenotata su Booking, che ci ha lasciati senza parole: una camera enorme e luminosa, con terrazzino privato e vasca idromassaggio fronte mare da cui ammirare albe e tramonti indimenticabili. Il letto comodissimo, la cabina armadio spaziosa e il bagno con kit di prodotti Occitane completavano un ambiente curato nei minimi dettagli. La pulizia era impeccabile e ogni sera ci facevano trovare dei cioccolatini in camera, un pensiero semplice ma molto raffinato che ci ha fatto sentire coccolati.

Per raggiungere la suite, situata in posizione panoramica, bastava richiedere alla reception una delle macchinette elettriche che ci accompagnavano comodamente su e giù, un servizio rapido ed efficiente che abbiamo trovato davvero pratico.

La spiaggia privata è un vero gioiello: sabbia finissima che sembra borotalco, mare trasparente e lettini molto confortevoli. Un consiglio? Svegliarsi presto, verso le 7, per accaparrarsi la prima fila e vivere tutta la giornata con la baia davanti, senza nessun ostacolo alla vista.

Un’esperienza che rende Redang unica al mondo è la possibilità di nuotare con le tartarughe marine adulte nel loro habitat naturale e, in certi periodi, assistere al rilascio dei piccoli direttamente dalla spiaggia: un’emozione che resterà impressa nella memoria di grandi e bambini. Molto suggestiva anche l’escursione di snorkeling nella baia vicina, popolata da una miriade di pesci colorati.

La colazione era ricca e variegata, con opzioni internazionali e locali. Per i pasti ci siamo spesso fermati al The Cove, il bar-ristorante sulla spiaggia: atmosfera rilassata, piatti gustosi e prezzi corretti (una margherita o un hamburger circa 12 €). Cenare con la brezza marina e il suono delle onde in sottofondo è stata un’esperienza che da sola valeva il viaggio.

Il personale è stato sempre estremamente gentile e disponibile, pronto a soddisfare ogni esigenza con il sorriso, contribuendo a rendere il soggiorno ancora più piacevole.un ringraziamento  speciale al referente Hamdan che si è reso sempre attento e disponibile per darmi consigli e farci sentire a nostro agio!

Abbiamo trascorso quattro notti indimenticabili, ma la sensazione, al momento della partenza, era quella di non voler andare più via. Siamo stati ad agosto il tempo è stato sempre perfetto per godersi il mare e le attività all’aperto.

Che dire: soldi spesi benissimo, un luogo che rimane nel cuore… ci tornerei domani stesso!

Leave me in this paradise!

The hotel enjoys a spectacular location, surrounded by nature and directly overlooking Redang Bay, a truly unique corner of the world that seems painted on paper. We stayed in a Cliff Bay Suite, booked on Booking.com, which left us speechless: a huge, bright room with a private terrace and a seafront hot tub from which to admire unforgettable sunrises and sunsets. The incredibly comfortable bed, spacious walk-in closet, and bathroom with a set of Occitane toiletries completed a space designed with meticulous attention to detail. The cleanliness was impeccable, and every evening they left chocolates in our room—a simple yet elegant touch that made us feel pampered.

To reach the suite, located in a panoramic position, we simply asked at reception for one of the electric machines that conveniently shuttled us up and down—a quick and efficient service that we found truly practical.

The private beach is a true gem: powder-fine sand, crystal-clear water, and very comfortable loungers. Any advice? Waking up early, around 7:00 a.m., to grab a front row seat and spend the whole day with the bay in front of you, unimpeded by anything.

An experience that makes Redang unique is the chance to swim with adult sea turtles in their natural habitat and, at certain times, witness the release of their young directly from the beach: a thrill that will remain etched in the memory of both adults and children. The snorkeling excursion in the nearby bay, populated by a myriad of colorful fish, was also very evocative.

Breakfast was rich and varied, with international and local options. For meals, we often stopped at The Cove, the beach bar-restaurant: a relaxed atmosphere, tasty dishes, and reasonable prices (a Margherita or a hamburger is around €12). Dining with the sea breeze and the sound of the waves in the background was an experience that alone was worth the trip.

The staff was always extremely kind and helpful, ready to meet every need with a smile, helping to make my stay even more enjoyable. A special thanks to our contact, Hamdan, who was always attentive and available to offer advice and make us feel at ease!

We spent four unforgettable nights, but upon leaving, we felt like we never wanted to leave. We stayed in August, and the weather was always perfect for enjoying the sea and outdoor activities.

What can I say: money well spent, a place that will stay in your heart... I'd go back tomorrow!

Ho trascorso un soggiorno splendido al Taras Resort di Redang, un’esperienza che merita pienamente 5 stelle.

La cosa che mi è piaciuta di più è stata la spiaggia privata: tranquilla, curata e con un mare spettacolare.
Nuotando, si può raggiungere facilmente il Turtle Point e nuotare insieme alle tartarughe, un’emozione unica.
I lettini sono ben posizionati e il servizio in spiaggia è eccellente: ti portano tutto quello che desideri, creando un’atmosfera di relax totale.

Un altro punto forte sono i servizi inclusi: yoga al mattino e al pomeriggio, una palestra meravigliosa con vista sull’oceano, kayak, biliardo, ping-pong serale, karaoke room… anche restando in hotel per più giorni senza fare escursioni, ci sono tantissime attività per non annoiarsi mai.

Le camere sono belle e confortevoli. Consiglio quelle con garden view o ocean view, che hanno la posizione migliore. Quelle con vista collina richiedono di prendere un transfer o fare parecchie scale, quindi sono da valutare in base alle preferenze e al budget.

Sul fronte ristorazione, l’hotel è pensato principalmente per un pubblico asiatico, quindi il buffet è ricco di piatti tipici locali (molto buoni: il roti e le uova scramble erano ottimi).
C’è anche un ristorante vicino alla spiaggia per la cena, buono ma non eccezionale, e un bar fronte mare meraviglioso, dove mangiare hamburger, pizza e drink con una vista incredibile.

Unica pecca per chi, come noi, viaggia senza bambini: ci sono molti gonfiabili e giochi sparsi per l’hotel, quindi capita di sorseggiare un aperitivo con bambini che saltano accanto. Sarebbe ideale creare una zona dedicata solo ai piccoli. Le piscine, spesso piene di bambini e di ospiti che fanno il bagno vestiti, risultano meno godibili. Inoltre, le nuove costruzioni di camere stanno un po’ rovinando il paesaggio.

In sintesi: un resort con mare da cartolina, tantissime attività e relax assicurato, perfetto per famiglie e coppie che cercano servizi e comfort. Qualche dettaglio migliorabile, ma l’esperienza complessiva è stata davvero bellissima
textTranslated:
I had a wonderful stay at the Taras Resort in Redang Island, an experience fully deserving of its 5-star rating.

My favorite thing was the private beach: quiet, well-kept, and with a spectacular sea.
You can easily swim to Turtle Point and swim with the turtles, a truly unique experience.
The loungers are well-placed, and the beach service is excellent: they bring you everything you need, creating an atmosphere of total relaxation.

Another highlight is the included services: morning and afternoon yoga, a wonderful gym with ocean views, kayaking, billiards, evening ping-pong, karaoke room... even if you're staying at the hotel for several days without going on excursions, there are plenty of activities to keep you entertained.

The rooms are beautiful and comfortable. I recommend those with a garden or ocean view, which have the best locations. Those with a hill view require a transfer or a lot of stairs, so choose based on your preferences and budget.

As for dining, the hotel is designed primarily for an Asian audience, so the buffet is full of typical local dishes (very good: the roti and scrambled eggs were excellent).

There's also a restaurant near the beach for dinner, good but not exceptional, and a wonderful beachfront bar, where you can enjoy burgers, pizza, and drinks with an incredible view.

The only drawback for those of us traveling without children: there are many inflatables and games scattered throughout the hotel, so you might find yourself sipping an aperitif with kids jumping around. It would be ideal to create a dedicated area just for kids. The pools, often crowded with children and guests bathing in their clothes, are less enjoyable. Furthermore, the new room construction is somewhat ruining the landscape.

In summary: a resort with picture-perfect sea views, plenty of activities, and guaranteed relaxation, perfect for families and couples looking for service and comfort. A few details could be improved, but the overall experience was truly wonderful.

We stayed here for 3 days and 2 nights (Monday to Wednesday in July). A day before our arrival, we called the hotel to inform them of our ferry arrival time. On the day itself, we were warmly welcomed by the hotel’s shuttle van driver as soon as we arrived. At check-in, we were greeted by a cheerful receptionist and offered a refreshing welcome drink - perfect for the warm weather.

We checked into our Garden Suite shortly after. The room was clean, comfortable, and inviting. We quickly brewed the complimentary coffee capsules provided in the room to recharge before exploring the hotel grounds and heading to the beach.

The beach was stunning - clean with soft white sand and peaceful, as it wasn’t crowded during our stay. We tried kayaking for the first time, which turned out to be a fun and enlightening experience. The next morning, we joined the 8 AM guided nature walk - a nice bit of exercise, especially for those of us used to sitting behind a laptop. The guides were friendly, attentive, and knowledgeable throughout.

During our stay, we enjoyed breakfast at the Asean All-Day Dining restaurant on both mornings. The buffet spread had plenty of choices - enough to spoil any appetite. The atmosphere at the resort was lovely, and the staff were consistently cheerful and accommodating.

For those using Maxis/Hotlink, signal coverage is strong throughout the resort. I had planned to get some work done - but with a beach that tempting, it was impossible to resist relaxing instead.

The beautiful weather, powdery sand, and turquoise-blue sea felt almost surreal - like stepping into a painting. We also explored Turtle Beach, which is just a short walk from the resort’s private beach. It was a fun little adventure.

A big thank you to all the amazing staff here - the drivers, the receptionists, the lifeguards, the snorkeling guides, the room service team, and everyone else who made our stay so memorable.

We only wish the trip could have been longer. We’d definitely love to return!

text: 7th to 13th of July 2025, What I appreciated most was the stunning white sandy beach and the spacious room with effortless beach access, which made things much easier while traveling with my one-year-old baby. A special mention goes to Hamdan, the room service assistant, whose kindness and attentiveness throughout my six-night stay at The Taaras truly stood out. The staff overall were warm and courteous, though I believe a touch more professional training would help meet the refined standards expected of a five-star resort. Among the dining experiences, both ASEAN and Merenero restaurant teams were welcoming, yet Merenero’s staff demonstrated a noticeably higher level of attentiveness. One memorable gesture was when I found myself without cash while waiting for the boat transfer—one of the staff not only guided me to the nearest ATM but personally took me there on his scooter, an act of genuine hospitality I won’t forget. On the less favorable side, the room furnishings felt outdated, with noticeable gaps that allowed lizards inside during my stay, and the towels were worn and rough on the skin. Breakfast lacked variety, leaving the experience feeling repetitive. Adding to that, aside from Hamdan, staff professionalism could be elevated; starting from Merang Jetty where I noticed staff smoking in the waiting area despite the presence of my baby, which felt far from appropriate. The same issue appeared at the scuba diving center, which is located right next to Merenero restaurant—I could even smell cigarette smoke while dining, something that diminished the overall experience. In summary, while I would gladly pay for the breathtaking beach alone, the overall cost—including flights, land and sea transfers, and the six-night stay—did not quite reflect the full value one might expect from such a resort.

text:
Kapalai is located approximately 45 mins to 1 hour from Semporna town, via a speed boat. It provides a 360° breathtaking ocean view. We were amazed by the unpolluted turquoise sea water upon arrival. The water is clean and see-through to the sea bed.

Sea turtles were abundantly spotted around the resort. We were told by one of the buggy drivers that Kapalai has its own man-made beach to encourage the sea turtles to lay eggs. To date, Kapalai has managed to release more than 100 sea turtles into the ocean. Sipadan is famous for its Green and Hawksbill sea turtles.

While snorkelling, we spotted not only sea turtles but barracuda, colourful coral reefs, stingrays, starfishes, squids, to name a few. The snorkelling gear can be rented for RM23/day. The famous clear kayak boat can also be rented for RM50/hour. This is especially famous amongst the ladies. The staff of Kapalai are more than helpful to help you take the best photos of you riding on the kayak.

"Harley-Davidson" could be rented in the resort for RM50/day. Don't get me wrong, it is however not the real Harley-Davidson, mind the pun. The staff refers the pastel rattan coloured bicycle as Harley-Davidson. The bicycle complements the beautiful resort. Aplenty of photos could be taken with you riding on it too.

Due to the previous case of resort guests being kidnapped by the Philippines pirates, whom subsequently demanded hefty ransom from the Malaysian government, Sipadan Kapalai Dive Resort is now safely and heavily guarded by the Royal Malaysian Navy.

text:
This is one of the most beautiful travel destinations that I have ever been to. At first, I was a bit skeptical about this Sipadan Kapalai Resort, because I have read through some bad reviews about the room condition. But I'm lucky that I don't have to go through all this bad experience. Each room is a standalone chalet that is built on top of the sea. I think some rooms are newer and some are slightly aged. But overall, I think the maintenance is quite good. My room is spacious and clean. Everything is functional. The Aircon is cold, but due to the hot weather, you will still feel heat in the afternoon and evening. As for the food, I think it is average. It is buffet style for all meals(breakfast, lunch and dinner). I think breakfast is the best because you hardly go wrong with fried rice, scrambled eggs, omelette or waffles. For lunch and dinner, the dishes are more suitable for locals. Anyway, don't worry about food running out if you are late to the restaurant. They always refill the food and there is always plenty of food left as long as the time is still within the buffet session.
The view at this resort is magnificent. I think the water is crystal clear, and you can always see a lot of fish swimming around the resort or beneath your room. It is like living on top of an aquarium. I'm lucky that I managed to see a few turtles swimming around in the early morning also. This is truly amazing. There are also sunset and sunrise point where you can take memorable photos and videos.
Overall, I am glad that I have visited this place. This is definitely one of the best places I have ever traveled to.

Disappointing Stay at The Taaras - Overpriced and Overrated

Our recent stay at The Taaras was a huge letdown from start to finish. It started at the jetty, where we waited in the hotel van for over 15minutes because it was blocked by other vans. We had to ask the drive and call hotel ourselves to sort it out.

Check-in was messy. Despite booking for 11 locals, the hotel insisted on collecting everyone's IC, which I think it's unnecessary. Then they claimed our package didn't include the Turtle Discovery, even though it clearly did. Thankfully, I brought the booking receipt.

Rooms were not well maintained i.e dirty staircases, faulty doors, broken kettles and fridges. The whole place didn't feel like a 5-star resort.

Activity arrangements were chaotic. We had initially reserved our Turtle Discovery activity for 9am the next day. Later, we were asked to shift to 10am, which we agreed to. However, when we arrived at 9:50am, we were told the booking was only for 10 guests instead of 11 and were asked to pay extra for one person. This was never communicated to us during check-in.

To make matters worse, we were made to wait even after 10am because they were not enough life jackets. It was frustrating, especially since all activities had been pre-booked, and the hotel should have arranged accordingly.

Another concern was housekeeping. When we returned from our snorkeling activity around 1pm, our rooms were still not cleaned. We informed the front desk, then went for lunch from 2-3pm. Shockingly, the rooms remained untouched.

Based on this experience, I find The Taaras to be highly overrated. The price we paid does not reflect the poor service, inadequate facilities, insufficient no of staff and disorganized activity arrangements.

This was my second visit to Redang Island, but my first (and likely last) stay at The Taaras. I love the island and will return, but I'll choose another hotel next time. The only thing I enjoyed during the stay here were the fire show and swimming with the turtles.

I hope this feedback is taken seriously.

This kind of place is absolutely surreal. It is definitely a must visit for those who appreciate pure natural beauty, isolation and the closest encounters you can get with marine life.

I will say that it is quite a far transport - you need to fly into Tawau airport, take their shuttle 1.5 hours to Sipadan, then ride a 45 minute boat. However, for what it is, you should visit.

Some of the resort guests are also quite loud and don't understand etiquette regarding quiet times or respecting the beauty of the surroundings.

text:
I am writing this review to strongly warn other travelers.

I stayed three nights at the Perhentian Island Resort (Pulau Perhentian Besar, Turtle Beach). During my stay, I suffered clear and medically confirmed bedbug bites. The symptoms started after the first night and worsened each day, showing the typical linear pattern. A pharmacist confirmed this, and I have photo evidence.

What is even more alarming than the incident itself is how it was handled. After I reported the issue, I was moved to another room for the final hours before my departure. This was not a gesture of goodwill, but simply the minimum necessary response. At the same time, I was told that no responsible person was available to make any decisions regarding compensation and that I should follow up by email. I clearly stated already then that this approach would likely result in the issue being denied later. Unfortunately, this is exactly what happened.

After my departure, the resort refused to take responsibility, claiming no evidence was found. I find it unacceptable that such a serious issue is being dismissed despite clear documentation.

In addition, I had significant effort and costs: medication, disinfection of luggage and rental car, and repeated laundry cycles — all during an ongoing international trip.

However, the core issue goes far beyond this single incident. This resort shows fundamental and systemic problems:
- Serious hygiene deficiencies (e.g. insects all over buffet food areas)
- Passive and disengaged staff despite high staff presence
- Lack of even basic safety standards

During a snorkeling trip, guests were not checked for their ability to swim. This led to two guests nearly drowning — they had to be rescued by myself and another tourist, not by the staff. I was personally involved and can fully confirm this.

These are not isolated failures. They indicate deep and ongoing mismanagement. Issues like bedbugs do not occur randomly — they are a consequence of sustained neglect.

Yes, the location is beautiful. But this does not justify risks to health and safety.

I strongly and explicitly advise anyone against staying at this resort.

I still expect appropriate compensation. If the resort continues to deny responsibility, I will proceed with legal action and involve the relevant authorities.

Avoid this resort!

Regards
Peter Schultze

text:
KAPALAI DESERVES MORE!

We stayed 6 nights and 7 days at this fantastic resort. I would like to share my experience so that those who choose this resort are aware of the significant limitations that unfortunately this magnificent structure presents.

Value for money 5/10
Considering a cost of about 650 euros per night for two people (High season - diving package with 3 or 4 dives per day), I wouldn't return to this resort.

The company policy is mainly oriented on the Asian market, and this choice affects numerous aspects that I will list here:

1. The transfer by speedboat from Semporna Port to Kapalai was not at all comfortable. We are used to the sea, and I understand that the weather conditions cannot be controlled, and there is an internal schedule to follow. However, I would like to emphasize that the boat was not suitable for those sea conditions; the rigid hull continuously slammed against the waves, resulting in a sore back. The captain could have easily reduced the speed.

2. Inadequate and unprepared staff. The management was careless in addressing various issues raised, and there was a total lack of authority in enforcing the necessary rules for civil coexistence and respect for this magnificent ecosystem and for those who wanted to spend relaxing moments.

2. Hygiene, cleanliness, and maintenance of the structure need improvement. The rooms are large and spacious with air conditioning, a fan, kettle, minibar, and safe, but a bit outdated. Maintenance is needed, especially in the bathroom. There are different types of chalets, some recently renovated. At the time of check-in, the room was very dirty, the wooden floor had not been cleaned, dust everywhere, especially on the shelves of the open wardrobe, and we even found a used soap in the shower. Towels were washed and fragrant but stained (despite being changed every day). Bird droppings on the balcony were not cleaned for days. Periodically, between 1:00 PM and 5:00 PM, maintenance workers start their work, and they don't care about the noise they make. The wooden planks of the pier that connect the rooms, since they are not properly fixed, make a terrible noise every time bicycles or golf carts pass near the room (this happens at all hours).

3. Environmental awareness and pollution control are non-existent. The showers in the rooms drain directly into the fantastic crystalline waters surrounding the resort, releasing polluting substances from the used soaps and organic waste (we even saw floating organic waste). Some areas of the resort's walkways are cleaned with bleach, which ends up directly in the sea after washing/rinsing.

4.Non-existent internet connection (this could be a plus for some). Wi-Fi is only available in the reception area, but it's very slow. Despite buying local SIM cards for data connection, the signal was completely absent for 2 days due to issues with the resort's receiver antenna
.
5. Good food for those who enjoy Asian cuisine. There is a total absence of continental dishes, only predominantly Asian cuisine with limited variety

text:
My partner and I spent 4 nights at Kapalai to scuba dive. Overall our experience was generally a positive one, but the 2-star review I'm giving is because on our final dive, after surfacing, our boatman Mustafa failed to see our signal buoy. It seemed as though he was sleeping, because the boat was completely idle for the next 90 minutes - there were no attempts to look for us, even though he well knew we should have surfaced by then. Our dive guide, Wei, also collapsed the signal buoy after about 3 minutes, and I had to plead with him to put it back up because it was obvious the boat had not seen us. Fortunately, luck was on our side and the current was pushing us back to Kapalai, but we swam for an hour to make it back safely. This could have been catastrophic if not for the current and where our dive site was. The manager of the dive center was apathetic to the situation and just directed us to the manager of the resort. The manager at least ended up comping our rental gear (~$180 USD for 2 people for 3 days).

Aside from that experience, Kapalai was very beautiful and well maintained. The staff weren't especially friendly, however. We were cautious with the food after reading other reviews from guests who had got food poisoning, and we fortunately had no mishaps. If you're not scuba diving, prepare to get bored after a few days, as there is not much to do aside from snorkeling around the house reef and kayaking in a small protected area.

text:
What a paradise and magical place. This is the perfect place for city dwellers especially newly weds or family with young kids to come over and wind down and de-stress and enjoy a dose of nature and sealife.

All meals were taken care of and you won't ever go hungry here with a wide selection of food buffet style over breakfast, lunch and tea time and dinner. My wife and I are vegetarians and they cooked us a great variety of food just for us every single meal. Food was a little salty so please request upfront if you're like us who don't like salty food.

Snorkelling highly recommended here. There were only 3-4 spots to snorkel but more than enough for us to see different species of fish. Highlight was the very friendly house turtle! He even came up and let us rub his back (or clean his shell maybe) and play and swim with him!

Room was slightly warm despite having an aircond probably because of the open space concept. There was a bathtub but not recommended to conserve on water usage.

Sunset was truly beautiful. So many spots and places to take photos and relax. Also very friendly staff who were patient in answering all our questions.

All in all highly recommended for everyone to come here and enjoy.

Tamppco está pensado para bañarse en el mar y descansar. Si te bañas no puedes tenderte al sol, Solo hay tumbonas en las habitaciones.

El agua color turquesa y los peces y fauna de vivos colores hace que sólo pueda recomendar, este resort a  amantes incondicionales del buceo, pues es lo único que se puede hacer.
textTranslated:
The resort is decent but a bit crowded for my taste. Personally, I felt a little trapped, as you're in the middle of the sea... in the middle of nowhere. Therefore, you can only sign up for scuba diving, either with or without tanks.
It's not really designed for swimming and relaxing. If you go for a swim, you can't sunbathe; there are only sun loungers in the rooms.
They also offer trips to a nearby island called Mabul, a 10-minute boat ride from the resort. Nothing special... a small village without much appeal, which you can see in 15 minutes.
The turquoise water and the brightly colored fish and marine life mean I can only recommend this resort to die-hard diving enthusiasts, as that's the only thing you can do.

The staff is very friendly, the location is simply magnificent, and there's plenty of space between the chalets, unlike other resorts. There are lots of animals—monkeys, squirrels, etc.—and we have a private beach. The à la carte restaurant is very good and reasonably priced, as it could easily overcharge us since there aren't many other options in the area. A dish costs between 20 and 30 ringgit. I highly recommend this resort for families or groups of friends. Note that it's not for people who want to party, but rather for nature lovers and those seeking peace and quiet.

text: This was my second stay at the resort, and once again, I had a great experience. The location is excellent, with beautiful surroundings, and the staff were friendly and very helpful throughout our stay.The resort has two restaurants, although the Thai restaurant was closed during our visit. The Jetty Paya restaurant is just outside the main gate and can be easily reached by buggy. The Sarang Seafood restaurant is about 2 km from the resort, and a return taxi fare is around RM50.Snorkeling trips to Coral Island, Renggis Island, and the marine park, as well as taxi services for going to restaurants, can all be organized through the hotel. You can also visit the marine park by taxi (suitable if traveling with senior citizens), which costs around RM100–150. Activities within the resort includes a game zone for kids, gym, pool table (4RM per game), bicycling, and kayaking. We appreciated the complimentary 1-hour bicycle ride provided by the staff.Breakfast was decent, but it would be even better with a wider variety of options. The room includes all the necessary amenities, but could be more modernized to better match the overall resort experience. The resort provided a complimentary minibar in two of the three rooms we booked, which was a nice added touch.Overall, it was another enjoyable stay, and I would definitely consider coming back again.

text: Come punto di forza c'è solo la posizione: su una bellissima baia con un mare stupendo. Per il resto il resort sarebbe da buttare giù e rifare completamente per quanto è ridotto male. Avevamo una stanza vista mare che cadeva a pezzi. Con degli scarichi dell'acqua aperti in bagno da dove entravano scarafaggi ogni giorno. E quella era la stanza migliore! Il cibo è disgustoso, per mangiare bisognava spostarsi in altri resort ogni volta! Il mare è bello ma è strapieno di barche che portano a frotte i turisti sopra 4 tartarughe ammaestrate che vivono lì. In spiaggia i lettini mezzi rotti in legno senza cuscini, quindi inutilizzabili. Incuria totale. E il personale non fa eccezione: antipatici e scortesi e anche ladri, visto che non mi hanno restituito il deposito iniziale e mi hanno preso in giro quando, ormai lontano, me ne sono accorto e gliel'ho segnalato! Ayuny è la ragazza che mi ha assicurato che mi avrebbero fatto il bonifico, ovviamente non è mai arrivato... complimenti! La ciliegina sulla torta! Andate alle Perenthian, possibilmente non in agosto ma non andate assolutamente al P.I.R.!! Ve ne pentireste amaramente!
textTranslated: The only strong point is the location: on a beautiful bay with a stunning sea. Otherwise, the resort deserves to be torn down and completely redone due to its state of disrepair. We had a sea-view room that was falling apart. The bathroom had open drains, and cockroaches were coming in every day. And that was the best room! The food is disgusting; we had to travel to other resorts every time to eat! The sea is beautiful, but it's packed with boats that bring tourists in droves on four trained turtles that live there. On the beach, the wooden loungers are half-broken and have no cushions, making them unusable. Total neglect. And the staff is no exception: unfriendly and rude, and even thieves, considering they didn't refund my initial deposit and mocked me when, far away, I noticed and reported it! Ayuny is the girl who assured me they would transfer the money, but of course it never arrived... congratulations! The icing on the cake! Go to Perenthian, preferably not in August, but definitely don't go to P.I.R.!! You'd bitterly regret it!

text:
Nous avions réservé 4 nuits au Perhentian Island Resort, mais nous avons dû quitter les lieux dès notre arrivée tant la chambre était dans un état inacceptable. Nous avons constaté la présence de cafards, de crottes supposées de souris, de moisissures, de toiles d’araignées, de poussière accumulée, ainsi que des murs tachés de sang d’insectes écrasés. Le sol était sale, et une forte odeur d’urine se dégageait du matelas.

Face à un tel manque d’hygiène, il était impensable d’y passer la nuit. Nous avons immédiatement décidé de partir et de séjourner au Marriott, qui était notre premier choix et qui, lui, offre un cadre irréprochable.

Je regrette d’avoir choisi cet établissement uniquement pour sa localisation, car il est tout à fait possible de profiter de la plage du PIR en séjournant dans un autre hôtel bien mieux entretenu et en s’y rendant simplement en taxi boat.

Ce qui est encore plus inacceptable, c’est l’absence totale de réponse de la part de la direction malgré nos nombreux mails concernant le remboursement des nuits non consommées. Ce silence en dit long sur le sérieux de la gestion et le respect accordé aux clients.

Je déconseille très fortement cet hôtel. Il ne mérite absolument pas sa réputation ni ses tarifs, et j’espère sincèrement que cet avis évitera à d’autres voyageurs la même mésaventure.
textTranslated:
We had booked four nights at the Perhentian Island Resort, but we had to leave immediately upon arrival because the room was in an unacceptable state. We found cockroaches, what appeared to be mouse droppings, mold, cobwebs, accumulated dust, and walls stained with the blood of crushed insects. The floor was filthy, and a strong smell of urine emanated from the mattress.

Given such a lack of hygiene, it was unthinkable to spend the night there. We immediately decided to leave and stay at the Marriott, which was our first choice and offers impeccable service.

I regret having chosen this hotel solely for its location, as it is perfectly possible to enjoy PIR Beach by staying in another, much better-maintained hotel and simply taking a water taxi.

What's even more unacceptable is the complete lack of response from management despite our numerous emails regarding refunds for unused nights. This silence speaks volumes about the seriousness of their management and the respect they show their customers.

I strongly advise against staying at this hotel. It absolutely does not deserve its reputation or its prices, and I sincerely hope this review will prevent other travelers from having the same unfortunate experience.

textTranslated:
The resort is huge!! The staff uses motorbikes to get around the grounds. The location is perfect, right in front of a beach where you can easily see turtles, all kinds of fish and baby sharks. The sun loungers are right in front, perfect for a sunbath in the sun.
If you are from Gavà, you have to go there to celebrate your wedding anniversary (Matilde, we love you ❤️😉).
As a negative point, the breakfast was too expensive for what they offered, but if you follow the road and cross the bridge, you will find very good places where you can have a good and cheap breakfast. At the Barat Hotel they serve alcohol, the only place in this part of the island (and they also give you ice cream if you know how 😉).
As a curious point, we would like to highlight that the cleaning and gardening service are "dumb", or so it seemed to us. They do not talk to the customers, but they always show you an angelic smile.
As a bonus track, you could almost swim with lizards in the pool, as they swim in the lake next door (it's NOT dangerous).

text:

En résumé : un hôtel qui se repose entièrement sur son atout principal — une plage exceptionnelle — mais qui gagnerait énormément à améliorer la qualité de ses prestations.
textTranslated:
The hotel boasts an undeniable advantage: its location. Situated on the most beautiful beach in the Perhentian Islands, the setting is simply idyllic. The snorkeling is fabulous: we were lucky enough to swim with several turtles, a stingray, and even some small sharks during our very first dip. Incredible!

However, the hotel itself is aging, and the service is clearly lacking. The toilet door blocks the bathroom door, the rooms weren't cleaned during our three-day stay, no extra towels were available without a charge, and no clean dishes were provided: we had to wash the cups and glasses provided for tea and coffee ourselves.

In short: a hotel that relies entirely on its main asset—an exceptional beach—but would greatly benefit from improving the quality of its services.

text:
Points ++

Mais présence de tortues, raies, requins, singes et écureuil !
Points - -
L'hôtel est à fuir, il est laissé à l'abandon, pas entretenu, les chambres jamais nettoyés! Juste mettre des serviettes, bouteilles d'eau et un coup de balai!
Présence de poussières, moisissures sur les murs, peintures et tapisseries dans un état horrible! Les meubles abîmés, lavabo cassé! Problème avec l'eau chaude! Les transats en bois ça vous casse le dos ! Le sable c'est mieux! Et si vous arrivez à en trouver un!
Car bcp de monde vient sur cette place, les transats sont censés être réservé aux guests de l'hôtel mais il n'y a aucune surveillance! Le restaurant est bof pas terrible, le buffet nul ils remettent les mêmes choses entre le matin, le midi et le soir résultat vous pouvez avoir des œufs de la veille avec mouches et fourmis autour! C'est froid! Le staff ne semble pas motivé, ils sont lents, on a l'impression de la déranger, ils sont désagréables (heureusement pas tous mais malheureusement la majorité)
Au vu du prix payés l'hôtel n'est pas à la hauteur c'est une honte !!
Le coral view à côté m'a l'air bcp mieux (à vérifier c'est une impression en y passant) il est juste à côté!
textTranslated:
Pros ++
The hotel's location is fantastic! Despite the murky water all over the island, it's not the Maldives!!

But there are turtles, rays, sharks, monkeys, and squirrels!
Cons -
The hotel is a disaster. It's neglected, poorly maintained, and the rooms are never cleaned! They just put out towels, water bottles, and give the place a quick sweep!
There's dust and mold on the walls, and the paint and wallpaper are in terrible condition! The furniture is damaged, and the sink is broken! There's a problem with the hot water! The wooden sun loungers are back-breaking! Sand is much better! If you can even find one!

Because lots of people come to this area, and the sun loungers are supposed to be reserved for hotel guests, but there's no supervision! The restaurant is so-so, not great at all. The buffet is awful; they serve the same things breakfast, lunch, and dinner, so you might end up with yesterday's eggs covered in flies and ants! It's cold! The staff doesn't seem motivated; they're slow, you get the feeling you're bothering them, and they're unpleasant (luckily not all of them, but unfortunately most). Considering the price we paid, the hotel is a disgrace! The Coral View next door looks much better (I'd have to check it out; it's just an impression from passing by). It's right next door!

text: Premetto che l’isola offre un panorama mozzafiato. Il mare è spettacolare con tutta la fauna marina che si può ammirare a pochi metri dalla riva. Detto questo, struttura, che dovrebbe essere la migliore e infatti è la più costosa, non è minimamente pronta ad accogliere turismo europeo. Cade letteralmente a pezzi, è sporca e abbandonata a se stessa. Le camere sono fatiscenti e con una scarsissima igiene. Lenzuola e asciugamani macchiati. Non è questione di sapersi adattare, perche quella non mi manca visti i molti viaggi in posti molto meno pretenziosi fatti negli anni scorsi. 40 gradi al sole e non si può bere una birra o qualsiasi tipo di alcolico da nessuna parte tranne in un bar gestito da personale cinese in un’altra spiaggia. La qualità del servizio è davvero pessimo. Merita venire solo per la spiaggia che è paradisiaca ma tre giorni sono più che sufficienti, se, lo ripeto, si possiede un grandissimo spirito di adattamento a sporcizia e odori. Peccato davvero perché avrebbe davvero grande potenziale vista la posizione. Infatti molti ospiti cambiano struttura non appena fatto il check-in. Ma essendomi informata credo che questa sia addirittura la migliore.
textTranslated: I'll start by saying that the island offers breathtaking views. The sea is spectacular, with all the marine life you can see just a few meters from the shore. That said, the facility, which should be the best and is in fact the most expensive, is not even remotely ready to welcome European tourists. It's literally falling apart, dirty, and abandoned. The rooms are dilapidated and extremely unhygienic. Stained sheets and towels. It's not a matter of knowing how to adapt, because I'm not lacking that, given my many trips to far less pretentious places in recent years. It's 40 degrees Celsius in the sun, and you can't drink a beer or any other type of alcohol anywhere except a bar run by Chinese staff on another beach. The quality of service is truly appalling. It's worth coming just for the heavenly beach, but three days are more than enough, if, I repeat, you have a great ability to adapt to dirt and smells. It's a real shame, because it would have great potential given its location. In fact, many guests change facilities as soon as they check in. But having done some research, I think this is actually the best.
