text:
Muy caro para lo que ofrece.
La playa en la que está ubicado será la mejor, vale, pero ello incita a que te encuentres todos los días con una llegada masiva de grupos que vienen a hacer snorkel y/o buceo, restándole la imagen de playa paradisíaca la que piensas que vienes. Aún así, la playa y hacer snorkel, valen la pena.

En cuanto al “Resort”, cutre, envejecido y mal cuidado. Falta de limpieza por todos lados, hasta las sábanas parecía que no eran nuevas de los huéspedes anteriores a nosotros, ya que había restos de arena en el interior de la cama…
Las cabañas tienen aire acondicionado y ventilador pero se les va la luz con facilidad. Agua caliente NO hay.
El desayuno es aceptable pero sin variedad si estás varios días. Y la comida no es de calidad… hemos estado probando los restaurantes de los hoteles cercanos y ofrecen mejores comidas/cenas.
Los trabajadores son correctos pero cero cercanía o simpatía (se salvan un par) pero mucha diferencia con el resto del país.

Sinceramente pagas un precio que no corresponde con las instalaciones.
Pagas por la ubicación.
De hecho teníamos solo 2 noches reservadas y nos quedamos más días en la isla pero cambiando de hotel.

Si tuviese que volver a esta isla desde luego no es un hotel al que vendría, le queda mucho por mejorar.
textTranslated:
Very expensive for what it offers.
The beach it's located on may be the best, sure, but that means you'll encounter a massive influx of groups every day who come to snorkel and/or dive, detracting from the image of a paradise beach you expect. Even so, the beach and snorkeling are worth it.

As for the "resort," it's shabby, outdated, and poorly maintained. It's filthy everywhere; even the sheets didn't seem new from previous guests, as there were bits of sand inside the bed. The cabins have air conditioning and a fan, but the power goes out frequently. There's no hot water. The breakfast is acceptable, but there's no variety if you're staying for several days. And the food isn't good quality... we've tried the restaurants at nearby hotels, and they offer much better lunches/dinners. The staff are polite but have zero friendliness or warmth (a couple are exceptions), but it's a huge difference compared to the rest of the country.

Honestly, you pay a price that doesn't match the facilities.
You're paying for the location.
In fact, we only had two nights booked and ended up staying longer on the island, but changing hotels.

If I had to return to this island, this is definitely not a hotel I would choose; it has a lot of room for improvement.
title: Perhentian Island Resort

1- The hotel restaurant is VERY much in need of improvement. The prices are a bit higher than in other areas, but that wouldn't be a problem if the food were good, but it isn't (except for a few specific dishes). It's clear that no one is in charge and there's no manager overseeing things. The breakfast is basic but adequate.

2- The rooms are the WORST part; they are completely unmaintained. The walls, closets, and floors are all worn and old. If that were the only issue, the rating would be higher, but no, they MUST IMPLEMENT CLEANING. There are no mosquito nets on the beds. Last night, we had to kill, without exaggeration, 15 tiny insects that I couldn't identify; they looked like tiny mosquitoes. Considering that we kept everything closed and shut the door immediately, it's understandable that you're in the jungle and there will be insects, but not in such large numbers. They should implement measures to prevent this. We paid €113 (for a standard room, not near the sea) per night, not €30. And what really shocked us was finding a large amount of some kind of grit under the bed. After investigating a bit, it seems to be termite droppings, I'M NOT SURE, but it wasn't sand. In conclusion, you don't sleep well.

3- The service: it's true that we encountered some pleasant people, but there were others who weren't particularly friendly.

I don't know if this is an isolated incident or not, since we haven't stayed at other hotels on this island. I don't know if it's common, but we stayed at Ombak Resort (on Kecil) and it was much better, both the restaurant and the rooms, and the service.

text:
We stayed at Coral View Resort but often wandered over to the beach in front of Perhentian Island Resort, as it turned out to be one of the nicest stretches of sand in the area. The beach here is wider and more sandy compared to other spots, making it much more comfortable for relaxing, strolling, or just lying down under the sun. The water is usually clear and calm, which makes swimming and snorkeling very enjoyable. Right in front of the beach lies Turtle Point, one of the best places on the island to spot sea turtles. With just a short swim out, it’s quite common to encounter these gentle creatures gracefully gliding through the water, which makes the experience unforgettable.

The only downside is that it can get rather busy at times, as boats frequently stop to drop off groups of snorkelers, which slightly disturbs the otherwise peaceful setting. Still, once you’re in the water, the beauty beneath quickly makes up for it. When snorkeling, don’t just stay at Turtle Point—be sure to swim toward the rocky areas on both the left and right sides of the beach. There you’ll find an abundance of colorful fish, vibrant corals, and even black-tipped reef sharks cruising gracefully in the shallows.

text:
If we could rate this resort higher than 5 stars, we absolutely would. After a long journey, our first experience at another place, Fauna Beach Resort, was so miserable and poorly maintained that we immediately started looking for an alternative. Thankfully, for a bit more money, we were able to book a stay at Perhentian Island Resort, and it turned out to be the best decision we made on our entire long vacation.

You have to remember that this is an island, and everything has to be brought in by boat, which makes the level of care and cleanliness at this resort truly remarkable. There are no highways, landfills, or hardware stores, yet they manage to keep everything in pristine condition.

This resort is absolutely fantastic and cared for down to the last detail. The breakfast was great, the rooms were clean and cool with air conditioning, and we received fresh water and towels every single day. The private beach with comfortable sunbeds is located right next to Turtle Beach, one of the most famous snorkeling spots on the Perhentian Islands.
Within walking distance is the wonderful restaurant The Barat, which offers delicious and affordable food. Unlike the resort's restaurant, they also serve a variety of beers, which was a nice bonus.

All in all, this was a fantastic experience. We would recommend anyone to spend a little more for this kind of luxury. The (slightly) cheaper Fauna Beach Resort was twenty times worse and practically falling apart. Count your blessings and go to Perhentian Island Resort; it’s worth every single euro!

address: Pulau Perhentian Besar, Besut, Terengganu, Malaysia
text: The last resort|Unfortunately, I whole-heartedly agree with previous reviewers. There are only two factors that keep the resort going - the wonderful beach and sea access, and the fact that - at least during the current high season - the demand for rooms is such that even very over-rated (and over-paid) facilities like the PIR get filled.  It sort of becomes the 'last resort' for people like us who do not book super-early and so miss out on any of the chain of much better places (supposedly lower grade) on this larger of the two islands - including Coral View, Abdul's Chalet, Mama's, Tuna Bay and several others.  All markedly better in most respects than the Perhentian Island Resort.  The place visibly dates back to the 80s, and much of it has not been renovated / updated since then.  No need to repeat what others have said - but just a few examples of the many seemingly little things that 'irked' us.  Breakfast - buffet type, but with low quality products throughout - old (non-fresh) chewy 'croissants', low quality juices, really almost undrinkable coffee... large round tables with unironed table-cloth that still have food remnants from the night before.  No ROTI CANAI - which is a major product produced and consumed for breakfast at the other, smaller resorts. Service people stand in corners of the room but are not helpful at all (except when collecting the pointless breakfast vouchers..).  There is an espresso / coffee machine - but when you ask, any 'good coffee' costs extra (different from 4 star hotels elsewhere).  - Rooms: no hot water (not essential here, but nice to have - available in some of the 'lower grade' resorts nearby).  No TV (again, not essential - but the others have it). Rooms all need to be 'redone' as well as thoroughly cleaned. - Staff - many are friendly and helpful enough, but generally do not seem to be trained well, or speak enough English for this kind of place.  Management / supervision overall seems to be lacking.  Example: we finally moved out to another resort.  The front desk is asked to call the other resort to send a boat. Staff tries once to call, then turns to us and says: no one answering the phone.  We try and immediately get someone and so arrange it all ourselves. - Anyway - our bottom line, and recommendation would be for the owners to do 2 main things: 1) to close the entire place for an entire season (or whatever it takes) to do a major overhaul of the entire facility, and 2) equally important, to seriously strengthen management and supervision, as well as retrain staff.

text: Io e mia moglie abbiamo soggiornato in questa struttura per 3 notti e sono pronto a dare il mio giudizio di come è andata l'esperienza: partiamo dal punto migliore che è l'isola, bella da vedere, in parte ancora rimasta selvaggia mentre nell'altra stragrande maggioranza invasa dalla mano dell'uomo per creare i vari villaggi adibiti al turismo. Ora passiamo alle parti peggiori di questo soggiorno: Il personale è completamente svogliato, sensa voglia di vivere, stanno li come se qualcuno gli puntasse una pistola alla testa, completamente apatici quindi nulli. Il ristorante di questa location va dal mediocre al pessimo il tutto a interpretazione personale, noi ci abbiamo pranzato tutti e 3 i giorni e devo dire che come cibo non è male, ovviamente non ci si può aspettare la cucina italiana però nell'insieme si mangia abbastanza discretamente ma per quanto riguarda la pulizia dei tavoli lasciamo perdere perché fa veramente schifo mentre il personale addetto come scritto sopra è inutile li devi chiamare per qualsiasi cosa anche per portarti il menù.. stanno li ti guardano con espressione da ebeti ma.non svolgono il loro lavoro, sbagliano continuamente gli ordini oppure si dimenticano le cose quindi per quanto riguarda la parte ristorazione mettiamoci una croce sopra con un piccolo punto di favore al cibo locale. Passiamo poi alle camere: ci hanno assegnato una stanza tipo la più distante dalla struttura dove per arrivarci ogni volta si muore di caldo non essendo raggiunta da nessun tipo di aria (nell'isola è veramente tanto caldo) una volta entrati nella casetta assegnataci la non pulizia regna sovrana, mobili vecchi e vetusti, le nenzuola del letto macchiate da una cosa non ben definita, finestre sporchissime, camera piena di insetti tra moscerini e fortunatamente poche zanzare almeno nella nostra. Macchie di sporco ovunque il condizionatore funziona bene per fortuna ma lasciato a se stesso nel senso che pieno zeppo di polvere nei filtri quindi si può immaginare la qualità dell'aria respirata.. abbiamo deciso di non contestaree tenere quella che ci  hanno dato, per il cambio asciugamani fortunatamente è stato fatto tutti i giorni rispetto ad altre recensioni. Alla fine posso dire che la spiaggia merita anche se alla mattina bisogna svegliarsi presto e mettere i propri asciugamani per prendere i posti migliori all ombra onde evitare di morire di caldo durante il giorno.
textTranslated: My wife and I stayed at this property for three nights, and I'm ready to give my opinion on how the experience went. Let's start with the best part: the island itself, beautiful to look at, some of it still wild, while the vast majority has been overrun by human hands to create various tourist villages. Now let's move on to the worst parts of our stay: The staff is completely uninterested, with no desire to live; they stand there as if someone were holding a gun to their head, completely apathetic and therefore useless. The restaurant at this location ranges from mediocre to terrible, it's all a matter of personal interpretation. We had lunch there all three days and I have to say that the food isn't bad. Obviously, you can't expect Italian cuisine, but overall, the food is pretty decent. As for the cleanliness of the tables, let's forget it because it's truly awful. The staff, as mentioned above, are useless; you have to call them for everything, even to bring you the menu. They just stand there looking at you with idiotic expressions, but they don't do their job, they constantly get orders wrong or forget things, so as far as the food goes, let's put a cross on it, with a small point for the local food. Let's move on to the rooms: we were assigned a room that was the furthest from the building, and it was scorching hot every time we got there, as no air could reach it (it's really hot on the island). Once we entered the little house assigned to us, the lack of cleanliness reigned supreme: old and outdated furniture, the bed sheets stained by something unclear, filthy windows, and a room full of insects, including midges, and fortunately, very few mosquitoes, at least in ours. Dirt stains everywhere. The air conditioning worked well, fortunately, but left to its own devices, meaning the filters were full of dust, so you can imagine the quality of the air we breathed. We decided not to complain and keep the one we were given. As for the towels, fortunately, they were changed every day, unlike other reviews. In the end, I can say that the beach is worth it, even if you have to wake up early in the morning and lay out your towels to get the best spots in the shade to avoid dying of heat during the day.

text:
价格与服务不匹配，不建议入住
我们于2025年7月25日（星期五）上午11:45抵达大停泊岛，但并无酒店员工迎接或指引。我们自行拖行李前往接待处后才得知酒店其实有行李运送服务，但并未在码头提供协助，实在不合理。

办理入住后被告知下午三点才能拿房，而我们的三天两夜浮潜配套第一场活动是在当天下午三点。多数酒店通常会弹性安排提前入住以配合行程，但这家酒店没有任何协调，只让我们寄存贵重物品。

浮潜结束后回到酒店，却发现行李被随意放在房门口。询问之下，工作人员称“不能随意进房”，但行李却能丢在无人看管的走廊两小时，无闭路电视保障，安全隐患极大。

入住后还发现冰箱里有半瓶喝过的水，明显房间未彻底清洁。而第二天虽然我们挂了“请勿打扰”牌子，外出浮潜回来后却发现有人进入更换了毛巾和水，前后政策矛盾。

泳池也未清洁彻底，底部明显布满污垢，令人却步。此外，酒店物价离谱，一罐普通汽水竟要RM9，远高于一般岛上酒店。

尽管大停泊岛本身风景迷人，我未来可能还会再来，但绝不会再入住这家酒店，服务水平与价格严重不符。

The price does not match the service, not recommended

After checking in, we were told we could only access our room at 3 PM, even though our snorkeling package likely had the first session at 2 PM. Other hotels typically allow early check-in for such cases, but no flexibility was offered here.

La salle de bain n'était pas propre ; la paroi de douche devenu opaque de calcaire, les carrelages sales ( mal nettoyé). La colonne de douche mal fixé au mur en était détaché. Ils sont venu "réparé " à ma demande mais ça bougeait encore. Le sol a été recouvert de latte de vinyl à coller de qualité mediocre; la saleté s'est incrustée entre les lattes. Ça ne fait pas resort du tout.
La piscine avait une eau verdâtre.
La plage est pris d'assaut par des touristes des autres Hôtels ainsi que nos transats. Les bateaux viennent y déposé des groupes en masse pour voir les tortues; on peux en voir à qq mètres du ponton. Pour voir du corail et des poissons il fallait aller après le ponton vers le Coral View resort.
La restauration était pas extraordinaire; assez répétitif. On a parfois pris en supplément à la carte. Les desserts par contre étaient relativement qualitatif ainsi que les petits déjeuner (il fallait juste demander du lait chaud).
Pas de WiFi dans les chambres (uniquement à la réception).
Point positif:
Ils distribuent sur demande des serviettes de plage.
Le personnel est très gentil.
La plage est magnifique.
Au final, si les bungalows sont mieux entretenus et que la restauration s'améliore, il pourrait être un très bon hôtel.
textTranslated:
The hotel is perfectly located on the most beautiful beach on the island. However, it's very old and in dire need of a quality renovation. The bathroom wasn't clean; the shower screen was covered in limescale, and the tiles were dirty (poorly cleaned). The shower column, which was poorly attached to the wall, had come loose. They came to "fix" it at my request, but it was still loose. The floor was covered with low-quality vinyl planks; dirt got trapped between them. It doesn't look like a resort at all.
The pool water was greenish.
The beach is overrun with tourists from other hotels, as are our sun loungers. Boats drop off groups of people to see the turtles; you can see them just a few meters from the jetty. To see coral and fish, you have to go past the jetty towards the Coral View Resort.
The food wasn't anything special; quite repetitive. We sometimes had to order à la carte as an extra. The desserts, on the other hand, were relatively good, as were the breakfasts (you just had to ask for hot milk).

No Wi-Fi in the rooms (only in the reception area).

On the plus side:
They provide beach towels upon request.

The staff is very friendly.

The beach is beautiful.
In the end, if the bungalows were better maintained and the food improved, it could be a very good hotel.

text:
I stayed for 3 nights with my 9-year-old son in the Superior Classic Double Room. Honestly, the room felt quite dated and in need of maintenance. At the very least, the resort should consider replacing the old door knobs, repainting the walls inside the room, and switching to brighter light bulbs.

The main reason I chose this resort was for the beach—and it did not disappoint. You’ll find soft, cotton-candy-like sand and clear seawater. With snorkeling gear, we were able to spot fish, small sharks, and even turtles right off the shore. The friendly squirrels were a delightful surprise—they aren’t shy and will come up to you asking for food.

The buffet breakfast was fairly decent, especially considering it was included with the room rate.

The resort's surroundings have a charming kampung (village) vibe, which I really enjoyed. However, do be prepared for large mosquitoes—bring insect repellent and mosquito coils for a more comfortable stay.

address: Pulau Perhentian Besar, Besut, Terengganu, Malaysia
text:
Wanna give my fair share of the review. Just been back for about a week.
Good things first. The most beautiful beach you can get on this island. Crystal clear waters and a view to behold. I love it to bits.

Rooms are very very basic, please be warned. This is no luxury hotel, not anything close to decent. It is very dated and poorly maintained. So be prepared that you are only here for a room to sleep in. Power trips are common, i guess it is some form of electricity saving policy.

Food's rather basic as well but sufficient if you take the buffet package. Ala Carte meals are rather pricey but that is expected. And do note that there's NO ALCOHOL serve or on sale on this resort which is entirely fine for families and most people. For those of you who want some drinks, my advice is to bring your own. Do buy enough drinking water at the Jetty before you come over to the resort. My suggestion so to buy a few large 1.5L bottles.

All in all depends on what you are in for, if the waters and beach are your top priority and everything else is secondary, then this is the place for you. If you prioritise decent accommodation and at an affordable rate, then you may need to look elsewhere.

Hope this help readers make informed decisions and managing expectations. I love this place just because of the beach, nothing else. Will I be back? yes just because of this.

address: Pulau Perhentian Besar, Besut, Terengganu, Malaysia
reviewContext/Rooms: basic and dirty.
text:
The experience was awful from the very beginning. Cleanliness was virtually nonexistent, both in the rooms and in the common areas. In the room, only the towels were changed (and they were old, torn, and stained), but the floor was never swept or mopped, and the bathroom was not cleaned. I had to repeatedly ask for basic supplies like toilet paper and soap. The mattress was extremely hard, making it impossible to rest properly. I reported it, but received no reply or willingness to solve the issue.
Housekeeping knocked on the door at 8 a.m. every day, regardless of whether guests wanted to rest a little longer. On top of that, there were scheduled power outages every morning and afternoon, which turned off the air conditioning and often disabled the hot water system — which already worked poorly via a button that sometimes didn’t respond at all.

Breakfast was extremely basic and unhygienic. The cheese was cheap, pre-packaged, and cut in half; the utensils were poorly washed; nothing was ever restocked. The dining area was dirty and clearly neglected, with spills, used plates, and a complete lack of organization.
The hotel is in visible disrepair: broken tiles patched with cement, rusty fixtures, litter in the garden, deteriorated furniture, and no visible maintenance of any kind.

The staff was unfriendly and uninterested. They never smiled or greeted guests, and acted like everything was a bother. I made several complaints — both in person and via WhatsApp, which is the only way to reach them — and none were ever answered. There is no phone in the room, and there is no Wi-Fi outside of the reception area, which is also not clearly stated when booking. Guests are given no information about the hotel or the island, and communication is practically nonexistent. If you have an urgent issue, good luck — no one responds.

The natural beauty of the location is the only positive thing, but that is not thanks to the hotel. The way this place is run is a total disgrace. I would strongly advise against staying here.
